    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline file_write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"who → World\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"input → 5\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(node --test \"$tf\" -- \"$DIR\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

Both run under Node's built-in `node:test` runner with\n  no extra dependency.\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` invokes them via `node --test` and folds\n  results into its pass/fail summary. The standard test entry point\n  (`bash scripts/run-tests.sh`) now reports 9 passing checks including\n  the two parser tests.\n- `SORAMECH_DIR=...` overrides the project root when running outside\n  the default install (argv would collide with `node --test`'s file\n  list, so an env var is the right channel).\n- Verified failure detection: temporarily breaking the Lua parser's\n  variadic-tail check caused the lua test to fail as expected.",
    "originalFile":"# 232 — Test coverage for `langs/<name>/parser.js`\n\n## Status\nin progress\n\n## Why this exists\n\nIssue 231 moved the per-language signature parsers out of the file\nbrowser and into `langs/lua/parser.js` and `langs/bash/parser.js`.\nIts own \"open questions\" section flagged the gap:\n\n> **Test coverage**: parsers are easy to break with a regex tweak. A\n> small set of fixture sources … and a JS test harness would catch\n> regressions. Out of scope for this issue, worth a follow-up.\n\nThis is that follow-up.\n\nIssue 217 part C will gate the editor's `var` toggle on\n`variadic_tail`. A silent regex tweak that mis-detects `...` or\n`\"$@\"` would re-introduce exactly the silent-error class 230 closed\noff — the editor would let the user wire variadic input into a\nfunction that doesn't accept it. Tests on the parsers' contract are\nthe cheap insurance.\n\n## Current behavior\nNo tests cover `langs/lua/parser.js` or `langs/bash/parser.js`.\n`scripts/run-tests.sh` only runs the phase-3 integration fixtures.\n\n## Intended behavior\n- Each parser has a paired `*-parser-test.mjs` test file in `tests/`.\n- Tests use Node's built-in `node:test` runner — no new dependency.\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` invokes them alongside the existing\n  integration checks; failures bubble up in the same pass/fail count.\n- Fixtures are inline strings inside each test file, not separate\n  files on disk. The parser's whole input is a string and the test\n  cases are short — externalising them just adds plumbing.\n\n## Test surface\n\n### Lua parser (`tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs`)\n- `M.concat(sep, ...)` → `variadic_tail: true`, `inputs: ['sep']`,\n  trailing `...` stripped from `inputs`.\n- `M.split(text, sep)` → `variadic_tail: false`, `inputs: ['text','sep']`.\n- `M.no_args()` → empty inputs.\n- Returns: bare identifiers become named outputs; expressions with\n  string literals or `..` collapse to `'result'`.\n- Block-depth tracker: nested `if`/`do`/`for` inside a function don't\n  trip the `end` matcher into ending the function early.\n- Empty source → empty array.\n\n### Bash parser (`tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs`)\n- Function with `\"$@\"` → `variadic_tail: true`.\n- Function with `local x=\"$1\"` → inputs named from locals.\n- Function with only `$1`/`$2` → fallback `arg1`/`arg2` naming.\n- Function with no positional args → empty inputs, `variadic_tail: false`.\n- Skips `if`/`while`/`for`/`case` keywords that look like function decls.\n- Single fixed output port `output` per the single-output rule.\n\n## Implementation steps\n1. Add `tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs`. Use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`.\n2. Add `tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs`.\n3. Wire both into `scripts/run-tests.sh` as a new section that runs\n   `node --test tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs`\n   and folds the result into the pass/fail count.\n4. Confirm both files run green; intentionally break a regex to\n   confirm a real failure is reported.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `langs/lua/parser.js`\n- `langs/bash/parser.js`\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh`\n- `issues/231-move-signature-parsers-into-langs.md` — the parent\n- `issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` — the consumer of\n  `variadic_tail`\n",

Phase 2 testing is ad-hoc: a few maps\n11\tin `maps/` (`hello`, `branch-test`, `classify-demo`, `driver-test`)\n12\tthat the developer runs by hand to verify the synchronous executor\n13\tstill works.\n14\t\n15\tPhase 3 changes the shape of the problem: many concurrent\n16\tinvocations, possibly thousands per run when iterators are in play,\n17\twritten from multiple worker threads. And the\n19\texisting maps cover only a small slice of the new surface (no\n20\tqueued inputs, no large iterator counts, no fan-in).\n21\t\n22\tThis issue covers two things that go together: the format and\n23\twriter for the run output, and the integration test plan that\n24\texercises the phase 3 runtime end-to-end.\n25\t\n26\t## Part A — Run output\n27\t\n28\t### Decoupling from the editor\n29\t\n30\tThe editor (phase 2) is being scoped down to a pure map editor — it\n31\tdoes not know how to run maps and does not display run results.\n32\t`last-run.json` is therefore not a UI feed. It exists for:\n33\t\n34\t- LLM consumption — agents reading the file to understand what a\n35\t  run did\n36\t- CLI-driven inspection — a future viewer utility (out of scope\n37\t  here) that pretty-prints the file\n38\t- Test harness consumption — the integration tests below diff the\n39\t  written file against expected output\n40\t\n41\tDecoupling means the writer's design is driven by these consumers,\n42\tnot by editor rendering needs.\n43\t\n44\t### File format: JSON Lines\n45\t\n46\tThe phase 2 single-document format does not work when the runner is\n47\tstreaming events from many threads. Use JSON Lines instead — one\n48\tJSON object per line, each line is one event, the file grows\n49\tmonotonically as the run proceeds.\n50\t\n51\tEvent types:\n52\t\n53\t```jsonl\n54\t{\"event\":\"run_start\", \"ts\":1234567890.123, \"map\":\"maps/classify-demo\", \"n_workers\":16}\n55\t{\"event\":\"task_submit\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"box_id\":\"classify\", \"worker_idx\":-1}\n56\t{\"event\":\"task_start\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3}\n57\t{\"event\":\"task_end\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3, \"duration_us\":127, \"output_size\":12}\n58\t{\"event\":\"slot_alloc\", \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5, \"size\":256, \"n_cells\":1}\n59\t{\"event\":\"slot_free\", \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5}\n60\t{\"event\":\"run_end\", \"ts\":..., \"duration_us\":1850, \"n_tasks\":7}\n61\t```\n62\t\n63\tJSONL is append-only, which makes thread-safe writing tractable: a\n64\tsingle mutex around the write call serializes the lines, and each\n65\tline is self-contained so a partial line on crash is recoverable\n66\t(reader skips the broken trailing line).\n67\t\n68\tThe reader (LLM, viewer, test harness) parses one line at a time;\n69\ttotal file size doesn't have to fit in memory.\n70\t\n71\t### What gets logged\n72\t\n73\tPer-task: submission, start, end, duration, output size. Inputs\n74\tand outputs are NOT logged by default — for iterator boxes\n75\tproducing thousands of invocations, logging every value bloats\n76\tthe file unbounded. There is a verbosity switch:\n77\t\n78\t- `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1` — log inputs and outputs (truncated past\n79\t  some byte limit, e.g. 4 KB) per task. For debugging.\n80\t- Default: log task lifecycle but not values.\n81\t\n82\tSlot allocator events (alloc, free, coalesce, grow) at a separate\n83\tverbosity level. Off by default; on under `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`.\n84\tFor diagnosing memory issues.\n85\t\n86\t### Writer mechanism\n87\t\n88\tA single dedicated writer thread inside the runner consumes events\n89\tfrom a multi-producer single-consumer ring buffer. Worker threads\n90\tpush event records (small fixed-size structs) into the ring; the\n91\twriter pulls them, serializes to JSON, and writes lines to the\n92\tfile. This avoids per-event mutex contention — the ring buffer is\n93\tthe only shared state, and a well-written MPSC ring is lock-free\n94\ton the producer side.\n95\t\n96\tAlternative considered: each worker writes its own log file, merge\n97\tat end. Simpler concurrency, but readers would have to merge by\n98\ttimestamp — and any cross-event reasoning (was task A still\n99\trunning when task B ended?) requires the merge anyway.\n100\t\n101\tThe writer thread is started after the pool is created and joined\n102\tbefore `pool_destroy`. It also handles `run_end` as the very last\n103\tevent, including the final summary.\n104\t\n105\t### File location\n106\t\n107\t`<map-dir>/last-run.jsonl` (note: `.jsonl` not `.json` — the\n108\textension reflects the format change). Overwritten on every run.\n109\t\n110\tA rotated archive (`last-run.jsonl.1`, `.2`, …) is out of scope.\n111\tUsers who want history copy the file before re-running.\n112\t\n113\t## Part B — Integration tests\n114\t\n115\t### Scope\n116\t\n117\tEnd-to-end tests of the pool runner against real map directories.\n118\tEach test is:\n119\t\n120\t1. A map directory under `tests/maps/<name>/`\n121\t2. An expected `last-run.jsonl` (or a comparison spec) under\n122\t   `tests/expected/<name>.jsonl`\n123\t3. A test driver script that runs the map and diffs\n124\t\n125\tThe test driver is `scripts/run-tests.sh`. It iterates\n126\t`tests/maps/`, runs each, diffs against expected (with a normalizer\n127\tthat drops timestamps, durations, worker indices — anything non-\n128\tdeterministic), and reports pass/fail.\n129\t\n130\t### Test maps\n131\t\n132\tCoverage targets:\n133\t\n134\t| Test map                  | What it exercises                                    |\n135\t|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n136\t| `hello`                   | Single Lua box, one input, one output                |\n137\t| `data-only`               | Data box → call box. No inputs, just stored values   |\n138\t| `fan-out-3`               | One output → three consumer boxes (peek, refcount)   |\n139\t| `fan-in-iterator`         | Three producers → iterator with queued input         |\n140\t| `comparator-routing`      | Comparator with all three branches (lt/eq/gt)        |\n141\t| `iterator-100`            | Iterator with 100 input values, round-robin to 3 paths |\n142\t| `multilang`               | One Lua box, one C box, one Bash box, all wired      |\n143\t| `large-output`            | Box producing a 1 MB string (variable-size heap)     |\n144\t| `cycle-detector-fail`     | Non-iterator cycle — load must abort                 |\n145\t| `missing-input-fail`      | Connection references a nonexistent box — load aborts|\n146\t| `box-error-fail`          | Box function returns nonzero — runner aborts         |\n147\t\n148\tThe `*-fail` tests verify error behavior — the runner is expected\n149\tto exit nonzero with a precise error message. The driver matches\n150\texit code and stderr against expected.\n151\t\n152\t### Test driver\n153\t\n154\t```bash\n155\t# scripts/run-tests.sh\n156\tfor test_dir in tests/maps/*/; do\n157\t    name=$(basename \"${test_dir}\")\n158\t    expected=\"tests/expected/${name}.jsonl\"\n159\t\n160\t    actual=$( \"${SOURCE_DIR}/soramech-pool\" \"${test_dir}\" )\n161\t    rc=$?\n162\t\n163\t    if [ -f \"${expected}.exit\" ]; then\n164\t        # *-fail tests: assert exit code and stderr substring\n165\t        check_failure \"${name}\" \"${rc}\" \"${test_dir}/last-run.jsonl\"\n166\t    else\n167\t        # success tests: diff normalized last-run.jsonl\n168\t        check_success \"${name}\" \"${test_dir}/last-run.jsonl\" \"${expected}\"\n169\t    fi\n170\tdone\n171\t```\n172\t\n173\t`normalize_jsonl` strips timestamps, durations, worker indices,\n174\tslot ids, and task ids (all non-deterministic) and sorts events by\n175\tevent type. The result should be deterministic across runs.\n176\t\n177\t### Phase 3 demo map\n178\t\n179\tA single map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/` that\n180\tdemonstrates everything working together:\n181\t\n182\t- Multiple entry-point data boxes\n183\t- Lua, C, and Bash boxes all wired together\n184\t- An iterator with a queued input\n185\t- A comparator routing into different downstream paths\n186\t- A large-output box (variable-size heap)\n187\t- Non-trivial graph topology (≥ 10 boxes)\n188\t\n189\tRun with `./run.sh` from the demo directory. Prints a short summary\n190\tof what happened (parsing the `last-run.jsonl`) so the demo is\n191\tvisible without a viewer utility.\n192\t\n193\tThis satisfies the standing project rule (CLAUDE.md) that each\n194\tphase produces a runnable demo in `issues/completed/demos/`.\n195\t\n196\t### Test infrastructure constraints\n197\t\n198\t- Tests must not depend on the editor or any HTTP server\n199\t- Tests must not depend on internet access\n200\t- Tests must run in under 60 seconds total on a developer machine\n201\t- Tests must be deterministic when normalized (any\n202\t  non-determinism is normalized out, not papered over with retries)\n203\t\n204\t## Open questions\n205\t\n206\t- Whether to log inputs/outputs by default. Useful for development,\n207\t  noisy for production. Current decision: opt-in via env var,\n208\t  default off.\n209\t- Slot-event logging: also opt-in. Useful for diagnosing memory\n210\t  issues. Off by default.\n211\t- File format: JSON Lines is the choice. An alternative was a\n212\t  protobuf or msgpack binary log, which is faster to write but\n213\t  harder to inspect by hand. JSONL wins on inspectability.\n214\t- Whether to keep timestamps as Unix epoch floats or ISO 8601\n215\t  strings. Epoch floats are smaller and easier to diff. Stick with\n216\t  floats.\n217\t\n218\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n219\t\n220\t### Run output (Part A)\n221\t1. Define the event struct and JSONL line format. Start with\n222\t   `run_start`, `task_start`, `task_end`, `run_end`.\n223\t2. Implement the MPSC ring buffer for events.\n224\t3. Implement the writer thread: pulls from ring, serializes,\n225\t   appends a line to the output file.\n226\t4. Wire event emission into the pool runner: `run_start` at\n227\t   startup, `task_start` and `task_end` in the dispatch action,\n228\t   `run_end` after quiescence.\n229\t5. Add the verbosity env vars and the optional event types.\n230\t\n231\t### Tests (Part B)\n232\t6. Create `tests/maps/` and `tests/expected/` directory structure.\n233\t7. Write the `hello` test as the first end-to-end smoke check.\n234\t8. Write the test driver `scripts/run-tests.sh` and the JSONL\n235\t   normalizer.\n236\t9. Add tests one at a time as each runtime feature lands. The\n237\t   `*-fail` tests can land before their corresponding successful\n238\t   tests if the failure path is implemented first.\n239\t10. Build the phase 3 demo map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/`\n240\t    once the rest of phase 3 is implemented.\n241\t\n242\t## Relevant files\n243\t\n244\t- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — test driver (to be written)\n245\t- `tests/maps/`, `tests/expected/` — test fixtures (to be created)\n246\t- `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/` — phase 3 demo (to be built)\n247\t- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — emits run_start / run_end\n248\t- `src/dispatch.c` — emits task_start / task_end\n249\t- `src/slot-store.c` — emits slot_alloc / slot_free (verbose mode)\n250\t- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n251\t- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — slot events\n252\t- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — task lifecycle events\n253\t- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — load-time errors\n254\t- `issues/309-build-system.md` — `make test` invokes this\n255\t- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — blocking semantics relevant to\n256\t  test design\n257\t\n258\t## Implementation log\n259\t\n260\t### JSON writer half — 2026-05-12\n261\t\n262\t`libs/json/json.c` had stub writer bodies left over from 314's\n263\tparser milestone; this pass filled them in. The writer maintains\n264\ta small depth stack (capped at 16) where each entry packs two\n265\tbooleans — \"next element is first\" and \"this level is an\n266\tobject.\" That's enough to handle comma placement and pick the\n267\tright close bracket. Overflow of the caller-supplied buffer is\n268\tsticky on `w->err`; `json_writer_finish` reports it.\n269\t\n270\tEight new writer tests in `tests/314-json-test.c` cover the\n271\tprimitives, escape encoding, empty and non-empty containers,\n272\tnesting depth, overflow detection, and a round-trip where the\n273\twriter emits an object that the parser then decodes and the test\n274\tverifies via the accessor API.\n275\t\n276\tStill ahead for 311: the JSONL event writer (a thin wrapper that\n277\tserializes `task_start` / `task_end` / `run_start` / `run_end`\n278\trecords using this writer), the MPSC ring buffer the worker\n279\tthreads push events into, and the dedicated writer thread that\n280\tdrains them.\n281\t\n282\t### Event emitters — 2026-05-12\n283\t\n284\t`src/013-jsonl-events.{c,h}` ships the per-event emit functions\n285\ton top of issue 314's bounded writer:\n286\t\n287\t- `jsonl_emit_run_start(w, ts, map, n_workers)`\n288\t- `jsonl_emit_task_submit(w, ts, task_id, box_id, worker_idx)`\n289\t- `jsonl_emit_task_start(w, ts, task_id, worker_idx)`\n290\t- `jsonl_emit_task_end(w, ts, task_id, worker_idx, duration_us, output_size)`\n291\t- `jsonl_emit_run_end(w, ts, duration_us, n_tasks)`\n292\t\n293\tEach emit serializes into a fixed 512-byte buffer, appends a\n294\tnewline, and writes to a `FILE *` under a per-writer mutex. The\n295\tMPSC ring + dedicated writer thread aren't there yet — the mutex\n296\tis a placeholder until dispatch is producing events fast enough\n297\tto justify the contention.\n298\t\n299\t`tests/013-jsonl-events-test.c` writes a full sequence, slurps\n300\tthe file back, and parses each line through 314's JSON parser to\n301\tverify the event shape. A concurrent-emit test runs 8 producer\n302\tthreads each emitting 200 events into the same writer and\n303\tverifies every line round-trips.\n304\t\n305\tStill ahead inside 311: slot-event opt-in\n306\t(`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`), inputs/outputs opt-in\n307\t(`SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`), the MPSC ring + writer thread, and\n308\tthe integration-test harness map fixtures.\n309\t\n310\t### Multi-producer event queue + writer thread — 2026-05-12\n311\t\n312\t`src/014-event-queue.{c,h}` ships the producer-side queue and the\n313\tdedicated writer thread. Producers (worker threads + the main\n314\tthread) call `event_queue_run_start` / `task_submit` / `task_start`\n315\t/ `task_end` / `run_end`; each emit appends a small fixed-size\n316\tevent record under a brief mutex and signals a CV. The writer\n317\tthread sleeps on the CV, snapshots the queue head into a local\n318\tbatch under the lock, then drains the batch outside the lock —\n319\tJSON encoding + fwrite happen with zero producer contention.\n320\t\n321\tFour unit tests in `tests/014-event-queue-test.c` cover single\n322\tproducer / multi-thread burst (8 producers × 250 events each =\n323\t2000 lines, all round-trip through the JSON parser) / shutdown-\n324\tdrain / pending-count.\n325\t\n326\tThe dispatch action (issue 304) opt-in emits task_start and\n327\ttask_end events with monotonic-clock durations via the queue;\n328\tthe pool runner emits run_start and run_end. `soramech-pool`\n329\twrites to `map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl` when that directory\n330\texists, falling back to `/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl`.\n331\t\n332\tWhat's still ahead inside 311:\n333\t- Lock-free Vyukov MPSC ring with sequence numbers — the\n334\t  architecture doc's preferred design. The mutex queue is a\n335\t  placeholder; upgrade once contention shows up.\n336\t- Opt-in slot events and per-task input/output dumps.\n337\t\n338\t### Integration test runner — 2026-05-12\n339\t\n340\t`scripts/run-tests.sh` runs every fixture map under `tests/maps/`\n341\tthrough `soramech-pool` and asserts the expected box-output\n342\tsubstrings show up in stderr. `make test` invokes the script\n343\tafter the unit tests so a full `make test` covers everything\n344\tfrom slot operations all the way through end-to-end Lua / C /\n345\tBash dispatch via JSONL logging.\n346\t\n347\tSix fixture checks at the moment:\n348\t- `calc`            — single Lua `add → 42`\n349\t- `hello`           — data → Lua, `greet → \"Hello, World!\"`\n350\t- `comparator`      — `high` fires, `low` / `mid` don't\n351\t- `iter-route`      — single-fire iterator picks `out_0` → `a`\n352\t- `pipeline`        — five-box multilang chain\n353\t- `pipeline file`   — verifies the file_write sink wrote\n354\t  `\"11!\"` to `/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt`\n355\t",

      "content":"# 311 — Integration tests & run output (`last-run.json`)\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nPhase 2 writes a `last-run.json` after every map run, recording per-\nbox invocations, inputs, outputs, and any errors. The editor reads\nit to display a run summary. Phase 2 testing is ad-hoc: a few maps\nin `maps/` (`hello`, `branch-test`, `classify-demo`, `driver-test`)\nthat the developer runs by hand to verify the synchronous executor\nstill works.\n\nPhase 3 changes the shape of the problem: many concurrent\ninvocations, possibly thousands per run when iterators are in play,\nwritten from multiple worker threads. The phase 2 \"build a single\ntable at end of run\" approach does not survive that. And the\nexisting maps cover only a small slice of the new surface (no\nqueued inputs, no large iterator counts, no fan-in).\n\nThis issue covers two things that go together: the format and\nwriter for the run output, and the integration test plan that\nexercises the phase 3 runtime end-to-end.\n\n## Part A — Run output\n\n### Decoupling from the editor\n\nThe editor (phase 2) is being scoped down to a pure map editor — it\ndoes not know how to run maps and does not display run results.\n`last-run.json` is therefore not a UI feed. It exists for:\n\n- LLM consumption — agents reading the file to understand what a\n  run did\n- CLI-driven inspection — a future viewer utility (out of scope\n  here) that pretty-prints the file\n- Test harness consumption — the integration tests below diff the\n  written file against expected output\n\nDecoupling means the writer's design is driven by these consumers,\nnot by editor rendering needs.\n\n### File format: JSON Lines\n\nThe phase 2 single-document format does not work when the runner is\nstreaming events from many threads. Use JSON Lines instead — one\nJSON object per line, each line is one event, the file grows\nmonotonically as the run proceeds.\n\nEvent types:\n\n```jsonl\n{\"event\":\"run_start\", \"ts\":1234567890.123, \"map\":\"maps/classify-demo\", \"n_workers\":16}\n{\"event\":\"task_submit\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"box_id\":\"classify\", \"worker_idx\":-1}\n{\"event\":\"task_start\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3}\n{\"event\":\"task_end\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3, \"duration_us\":127, \"output_size\":12}\n{\"event\":\"slot_alloc\", \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5, \"size\":256, \"n_cells\":1}\n{\"event\":\"slot_free\", \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5}\n{\"event\":\"run_end\", \"ts\":..., \"duration_us\":1850, \"n_tasks\":7}\n```\n\nJSONL is append-only, which makes thread-safe writing tractable: a\nsingle mutex around the write call serializes the lines, and each\nline is self-contained so a partial line on crash is recoverable\n(reader skips the broken trailing line).\n\nThe reader (LLM, viewer, test harness) parses one line at a time;\ntotal file size doesn't have to fit in memory.\n\n### What gets logged\n\nPer-task: submission, start, end, duration, output size. Inputs\nand outputs are NOT logged by default — for iterator boxes\nproducing thousands of invocations, logging every value bloats\nthe file unbounded. There is a verbosity switch:\n\n- `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1` — log inputs and outputs (truncated past\n  some byte limit, e.g. 4 KB) per task. For debugging.\n- Default: log task lifecycle but not values.\n\nSlot allocator events (alloc, free, coalesce, grow) at a separate\nverbosity level. Off by default; on under `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`.\nFor diagnosing memory issues.\n\n### Writer mechanism\n\nA single dedicated writer thread inside the runner consumes events\nfrom a multi-producer single-consumer ring buffer. Worker threads\npush event records (small fixed-size structs) into the ring; the\nwriter pulls them, serializes to JSON, and writes lines to the\nfile. This avoids per-event mutex contention — the ring buffer is\nthe only shared state, and a well-written MPSC ring is lock-free\non the producer side.\n\nAlternative considered: each worker writes its own log file, merge\nat end. Simpler concurrency, but readers would have to merge by\ntimestamp — and any cross-event reasoning (was task A still\nrunning when task B ended?) requires the merge anyway.\n\nThe writer thread is started after the pool is created and joined\nbefore `pool_destroy`. It also handles `run_end` as the very last\nevent, including the final summary.\n\n### File location\n\n`<map-dir>/last-run.jsonl` (note: `.jsonl` not `.json` — the\nextension reflects the format change). Overwritten on every run.\n\nA rotated archive (`last-run.jsonl.1`, `.2`, …) is out of scope.\nUsers who want history copy the file before re-running.\n\n## Part B — Integration tests\n\n### Scope\n\nEnd-to-end tests of the pool runner against real map directories.\nEach test is:\n\n1. A map directory under `tests/maps/<name>/`\n2. An expected `last-run.jsonl` (or a comparison spec) under\n   `tests/expected/<name>.jsonl`\n3. A test driver script that runs the map and diffs\n\nThe test driver is `scripts/run-tests.sh`. It iterates\n`tests/maps/`, runs each, diffs against expected (with a normalizer\nthat drops timestamps, durations, worker indices — anything non-\ndeterministic), and reports pass/fail.\n\n### Test maps\n\nCoverage targets:\n\n| Test map                  | What it exercises                                    |\n|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| `hello`                   | Single Lua box, one input, one output                |\n| `data-only`               | Data box → call box. No inputs, just stored values   |\n| `fan-out-3`               | One output → three consumer boxes (peek, refcount)   |\n| `fan-in-iterator`         | Three producers → iterator with queued input         |\n| `comparator-routing`      | Comparator with all three branches (lt/eq/gt)        |\n| `iterator-100`            | Iterator with 100 input values, round-robin to 3 paths |\n| `multilang`               | One Lua box, one C box, one Bash box, all wired      |\n| `large-output`            | Box producing a 1 MB string (variable-size heap)     |\n| `cycle-detector-fail`     | Non-iterator cycle — load must abort                 |\n| `missing-input-fail`      | Connection references a nonexistent box — load aborts|\n| `box-error-fail`          | Box function returns nonzero — runner aborts         |\n\nThe `*-fail` tests verify error behavior — the runner is expected\nto exit nonzero with a precise error message. The driver matches\nexit code and stderr against expected.\n\n### Test driver\n\n```bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh\nfor test_dir in tests/maps/*/; do\n    name=$(basename \"${test_dir}\")\n    expected=\"tests/expected/${name}.jsonl\"\n\n    actual=$( \"${SOURCE_DIR}/soramech-pool\" \"${test_dir}\" )\n    rc=$?\n\n    if [ -f \"${expected}.exit\" ]; then\n        # *-fail tests: assert exit code and stderr substring\n        check_failure \"${name}\" \"${rc}\" \"${test_dir}/last-run.jsonl\"\n    else\n        # success tests: diff normalized last-run.jsonl\n        check_success \"${name}\" \"${test_dir}/last-run.jsonl\" \"${expected}\"\n    fi\ndone\n```\n\n`normalize_jsonl` strips timestamps, durations, worker indices,\nslot ids, and task ids (all non-deterministic) and sorts events by\nevent type. The result should be deterministic across runs.\n\n### Phase 3 demo map\n\nA single map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/` that\ndemonstrates everything working together:\n\n- Multiple entry-point data boxes\n- Lua, C, and Bash boxes all wired together\n- An iterator with a queued input\n- A comparator routing into different downstream paths\n- A large-output box (variable-size heap)\n- Non-trivial graph topology (≥ 10 boxes)\n\nRun with `./run.sh` from the demo directory. Prints a short summary\nof what happened (parsing the `last-run.jsonl`) so the demo is\nvisible without a viewer utility.\n\nThis satisfies the standing project rule (CLAUDE.md) that each\nphase produces a runnable demo in `issues/completed/demos/`.\n\n### Test infrastructure constraints\n\n- Tests must not depend on the editor or any HTTP server\n- Tests must not depend on internet access\n- Tests must run in under 60 seconds total on a developer machine\n- Tests must be deterministic when normalized (any\n  non-determinism is normalized out, not papered over with retries)\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Whether to log inputs/outputs by default. Useful for development,\n  noisy for production. Current decision: opt-in via env var,\n  default off.\n- Slot-event logging: also opt-in. Useful for diagnosing memory\n  issues. Off by default.\n- File format: JSON Lines is the choice. An alternative was a\n  protobuf or msgpack binary log, which is faster to write but\n  harder to inspect by hand. JSONL wins on inspectability.\n- Whether to keep timestamps as Unix epoch floats or ISO 8601\n  strings. Epoch floats are smaller and easier to diff. Stick with\n  floats.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n### Run output (Part A)\n1. Define the event struct and JSONL line format. Start with\n   `run_start`, `task_start`, `task_end`, `run_end`.\n2. Implement the MPSC ring buffer for events.\n3. Implement the writer thread: pulls from ring, serializes,\n   appends a line to the output file.\n4. Wire event emission into the pool runner: `run_start` at\n   startup, `task_start` and `task_end` in the dispatch action,\n   `run_end` after quiescence.\n5. Add the verbosity env vars and the optional event types.\n\n### Tests (Part B)\n6. Create `tests/maps/` and `tests/expected/` directory structure.\n7. Write the `hello` test as the first end-to-end smoke check.\n8. Write the test driver `scripts/run-tests.sh` and the JSONL\n   normalizer.\n9. Add tests one at a time as each runtime feature lands. The\n   `*-fail` tests can land before their corresponding successful\n   tests if the failure path is implemented first.\n10. Build the phase 3 demo map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/`\n    once the rest of phase 3 is implemented.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — test driver (to be written)\n- `tests/maps/`, `tests/expected/` — test fixtures (to be created)\n- `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/` — phase 3 demo (to be built)\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — emits run_start / run_end\n- `src/dispatch.c` — emits task_start / task_end\n- `src/slot-store.c` — emits slot_alloc / slot_free (verbose mode)\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — slot events\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — task lifecycle events\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — load-time errors\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — `make test` invokes this\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — blocking semantics relevant to\n  test design\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### JSON writer half — 2026-05-12\n\n`libs/json/json.c` had stub writer bodies left over from 314's\nparser milestone; this pass filled them in. The writer maintains\na small depth stack (capped at 16) where each entry packs two\nbooleans — \"next element is first\" and \"this level is an\nobject.\" That's enough to handle comma placement and pick the\nright close bracket. Overflow of the caller-supplied buffer is\nsticky on `w->err`; `json_writer_finish` reports it.\n\nEight new writer tests in `tests/314-json-test.c` cover the\nprimitives, escape encoding, empty and non-empty containers,\nnesting depth, overflow detection, and a round-trip where the\nwriter emits an object that the parser then decodes and the test\nverifies via the accessor API.\n\nStill ahead for 311: the JSONL event writer (a thin wrapper that\nserializes `task_start` / `task_end` / `run_start` / `run_end`\nrecords using this writer), the MPSC ring buffer the worker\nthreads push events into, and the dedicated writer thread that\ndrains them.\n\n### Event emitters — 2026-05-12\n\n`src/013-jsonl-events.{c,h}` ships the per-event emit functions\non top of issue 314's bounded writer:\n\n- `jsonl_emit_run_start(w, ts, map, n_workers)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_submit(w, ts, task_id, box_id, worker_idx)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_start(w, ts, task_id, worker_idx)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_end(w, ts, task_id, worker_idx, duration_us, output_size)`\n- `jsonl_emit_run_end(w, ts, duration_us, n_tasks)`\n\nEach emit serializes into a fixed 512-byte buffer, appends a\nnewline, and writes to a `FILE *` under a per-writer mutex. The\nMPSC ring + dedicated writer thread aren't there yet — the mutex\nis a placeholder until dispatch is producing events fast enough\nto justify the contention.\n\n`tests/013-jsonl-events-test.c` writes a full sequence, slurps\nthe file back, and parses each line through 314's JSON parser to\nverify the event shape. A concurrent-emit test runs 8 producer\nthreads each emitting 200 events into the same writer and\nverifies every line round-trips.\n\nStill ahead inside 311: slot-event opt-in\n(`SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`), inputs/outputs opt-in\n(`SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1`), the MPSC ring + writer thread, and\nthe integration-test harness map fixtures.\n\n### Multi-producer event queue + writer thread — 2026-05-12\n\n`src/014-event-queue.{c,h}` ships the producer-side queue and the\ndedicated writer thread. Producers (worker threads + the main\nthread) call `event_queue_run_start` / `task_submit` / `task_start`\n/ `task_end` / `run_end`; each emit appends a small fixed-size\nevent record under a brief mutex and signals a CV. The writer\nthread sleeps on the CV, snapshots the queue head into a local\nbatch under the lock, then drains the batch outside the lock —\nJSON encoding + fwrite happen with zero producer contention.\n\nFour unit tests in `tests/014-event-queue-test.c` cover single\nproducer / multi-thread burst (8 producers × 250 events each =\n2000 lines, all round-trip through the JSON parser) / shutdown-\ndrain / pending-count.\n\nThe dispatch action (issue 304) opt-in emits task_start and\ntask_end events with monotonic-clock durations via the queue;\nthe pool runner emits run_start and run_end. `soramech-pool`\nwrites to `map_dir/tmp/last-run.jsonl` when that directory\nexists, falling back to `/tmp/soramech-last-run.jsonl`.\n\nWhat's still ahead inside 311:\n- Lock-free Vyukov MPSC ring with sequence numbers — the\n  architecture doc's preferred design. The mutex queue is a\n  placeholder; upgrade once contention shows up.\n- Opt-in slot events and per-task input/output dumps.\n\n### Integration test runner — 2026-05-12\n\n`scripts/run-tests.sh` runs every fixture map under `tests/maps/`\nthrough `soramech-pool` and asserts the expected box-output\nsubstrings show up in stderr. `make test` invokes the script\nafter the unit tests so a full `make test` covers everything\nfrom slot operations all the way through end-to-end Lua / C /\nBash dispatch via JSONL logging.\n\nSix fixture checks at the moment:\n- `calc`            — single Lua `add → 42`\n- `hello`           — data → Lua, `greet → \"Hello, World!\"`\n- `comparator`      — `high` fires, `low` / `mid` don't\n- `iter-route`      — single-fire iterator picks `out_0` → `a`\n- `pipeline`        — five-box multilang chain\n- `pipeline file`   — verifies the file_write sink wrote\n  `\"11!\"` to `/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt`\n",

    "originalFile":"# 232 — Test coverage for `langs/<name>/parser.js`\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Resolution\n\n- `tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs` (10 cases) and\n  `tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs` (9 cases) cover the parser\n  contracts. Both run under Node's built-in `node:test` runner with\n  no extra dependency.\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` invokes them via `node --test` and folds\n  results into its pass/fail summary. The standard test entry point\n  (`bash scripts/run-tests.sh`) now reports 9 passing checks including\n  the two parser tests.\n- `SORAMECH_DIR=...` overrides the project root when running outside\n  the default install (argv would collide with `node --test`'s file\n  list, so an env var is the right channel).\n- Verified failure detection: temporarily breaking the Lua parser's\n  variadic-tail check caused the lua test to fail as expected.\n\n## Why this exists\n\nIssue 231 moved the per-language signature parsers out of the file\nbrowser and into `langs/lua/parser.js` and `langs/bash/parser.js`.\nIts own \"open questions\" section flagged the gap:\n\n> **Test coverage**: parsers are easy to break with a regex tweak. A\n> small set of fixture sources … and a JS test harness would catch\n> regressions. Out of scope for this issue, worth a follow-up.\n\nThis is that follow-up.\n\nIssue 217 part C will gate the editor's `var` toggle on\n`variadic_tail`. A silent regex tweak that mis-detects `...` or\n`\"$@\"` would re-introduce exactly the silent-error class 230 closed\noff — the editor would let the user wire variadic input into a\nfunction that doesn't accept it. Tests on the parsers' contract are\nthe cheap insurance.\n\n## Current behavior\nNo tests cover `langs/lua/parser.js` or `langs/bash/parser.js`.\n`scripts/run-tests.sh` only runs the phase-3 integration fixtures.\n\n## Intended behavior\n- Each parser has a paired `*-parser-test.mjs` test file in `tests/`.\n- Tests use Node's built-in `node:test` runner — no new dependency.\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` invokes them alongside the existing\n  integration checks; failures bubble up in the same pass/fail count.\n- Fixtures are inline strings inside each test file, not separate\n  files on disk. The parser's whole input is a string and the test\n  cases are short — externalising them just adds plumbing.\n\n## Test surface\n\n### Lua parser (`tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs`)\n- `M.concat(sep, ...)` → `variadic_tail: true`, `inputs: ['sep']`,\n  trailing `...` stripped from `inputs`.\n- `M.split(text, sep)` → `variadic_tail: false`, `inputs: ['text','sep']`.\n- `M.no_args()` → empty inputs.\n- Returns: bare identifiers become named outputs; expressions with\n  string literals or `..` collapse to `'result'`.\n- Block-depth tracker: nested `if`/`do`/`for` inside a function don't\n  trip the `end` matcher into ending the function early.\n- Empty source → empty array.\n\n### Bash parser (`tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs`)\n- Function with `\"$@\"` → `variadic_tail: true`.\n- Function with `local x=\"$1\"` → inputs named from locals.\n- Function with only `$1`/`$2` → fallback `arg1`/`arg2` naming.\n- Function with no positional args → empty inputs, `variadic_tail: false`.\n- Skips `if`/`while`/`for`/`case` keywords that look like function decls.\n- Single fixed output port `output` per the single-output rule.\n\n## Implementation steps\n1. Add `tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs`. Use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`.\n2. Add `tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs`.\n3. Wire both into `scripts/run-tests.sh` as a new section that runs\n   `node --test tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs`\n   and folds the result into the pass/fail count.\n4. Confirm both files run green; intentionally break a regex to\n   confirm a real failure is reported.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `langs/lua/parser.js`\n- `langs/bash/parser.js`\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh`\n- `issues/231-move-signature-parsers-into-langs.md` — the parent\n- `issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` — the consumer of\n  `variadic_tail`\n",

    "originalFile":"# 232 — Test coverage map\n\n## Status\nongoing (test inventory; updated each time tests are added or\nremoved)\n\n## Why this exists\n\nThe project already has two test-infrastructure issues, both\nfocused on phase-3 C runtime concerns:\n\n- **311** — integration-test driver and the JSONL run-output\n  format. Without that view, gaps accumulate silently: tests get\nwritten for the area someone happens to be touching, the rest\ndrifts uncovered. When a new module is added, a row goes\ninto the appropriate section showing it has no coverage yet.\n\n## How to read the table\n\n- `[x]` — has a dedicated test file (path in the row).\n- `[ ]` — no dedicated test; may be exercised indirectly through\n  integration fixtures, but not directly verified.\n- `[~]` — partially covered; only some surface area is tested.\n- `[—]` — intentionally untested (vendored library, thin entrypoint, etc.).\n\n## Editor side — JavaScript\n\nThe editor is a browser app served by `src/005-http-server.lua`.\nNo JS test runner was wired up before the work that opened this\nissue; the parser tests introduced one (Node's built-in\n`node:test`). Other JS modules can follow the same pattern when\nthey get tests.\n\n| Module | Coverage | Test file |\n|---|---|---|\n| `langs/lua/parser.js` | `[x]` | `tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs` |\n| `langs/bash/parser.js` | `[x]` | `tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs` |\n| `langs/c/parser.js` | `[—]` | not written yet; issue 231 makes it optional |\n| `langs/lua/lexer.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `langs/bash/lexer.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `langs/c/lexer.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `assets/js/001-canvas.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `assets/js/002-boxes.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `assets/js/003-api.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `assets/js/004-inspector.js` | `[ ]` | — (variadic helpers are pure functions, prime unit-test candidates) |\n| `assets/js/005-app.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `assets/js/006-wires.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `assets/js/008-source-view.js` | `[ ]` | — |\n\nHighest-value next targets: the variadic-slot helpers in\n`004-inspector.js` (pure functions, no DOM dependency, directly\nconsumed by issue 217 part C) and the lexer registries in the\nlanguage directories.\n\n## Lua libraries — `libs/*.lua`\n\n| Module | Coverage | Test file |\n|---|---|---|\n| `libs/soramech-data.lua` | `[x]` | `tests/003-data-test.lua` |\n| `libs/text.lua` | `[ ]` | — (issue 237 expanded the surface: concat, split, upper, lower, trim, replace, replace_first, contains, starts_with, ends_with, length, substring) |\n| `libs/files.lua` | `[ ]` | — |\n| `libs/ollama.lua` | `[—]` | requires a live Ollama endpoint; no unit-level coverage |\n| `src/005-http-server.lua` | `[ ]` | — (GET/PUT boxes, connections, files, source) |\n| `src/006-server-main.lua` | `[—]` | thin entrypoint |\n| `src/007-runner-main.lua` | `[—]` | thin entrypoint |\n\nSchema and validator are the highest-value gaps — they are the\nlast line of defense against malformed map files and they're pure\nfunctions over JSON-shaped tables, very testable.\n\n## C runtime — `src/*.c`\n\nBest-covered area of the project; Under a second on a current build.","+2. **Continues past failures.** Every binary runs; summary at the","+   bottom names what went wrong.","+3. **Pretty by default, mineable on request.** Per-binary one-line","+   status by default; `--quiet` prints only totals; `--verbose`","+   dumps each binary's full output.","+4. **Filterable.** `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh 009` runs only","+   binaries whose names start with `009`.","+","+Concept: glob `build/tests/<name>-test`, sort by filename (which","+sorts by the project's leading numeric index), run each in turn,","+capture stdout/stderr, parse the binary's trailing","+`N passed, M failed` line for the verdict.","+","+Output shape:","+```","+  009-slot-store-test                          16 / 16  ok","+  010-graph-loader-test                        13 / 13  ok","+  015-large-value-heap-test                     8 /  8  ok","+  ...","+  113 / 113 tests passed (14 binaries)","+```","+","+A failing binary prints its captured output below the summary","+line. Exit code is zero iff every binary passes; non-zero with the","+count of failing binaries otherwise.","+","+Convention compliance per CLAUDE.md: hard-coded `${DIR}` at top","+with arg override, all paths under `${DIR}`, each shell command on","+its own line, lives at `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh`.","+","+Open question (from 316): should the script warn when a binary's","+source is newer than the binary? Cheap (`stat` both sides), but","+the default should be \"just run what's built\" — offer it as","+`--check-stale`.","+","+### Implementation steps for the new runner","+1. Write `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh` with the layout above.","+2. Verify it picks up every existing `build/tests/*-test` binary","+   and produces the expected totals.","+3. Verify `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh 015` filters to one binary.","+4. Verify `--quiet` and `--verbose` produce useful output.","+5.     "userModified":false,
    "newString":"# 316 — Simple test runner script\n\n## Status\nfolded into issue 232 (test coverage map)\n\n## Resolution\n\nThe scope of this issue — a build-free unit-test runner script at\n`scripts/run-unit-tests.sh` — was folded into issue 232's\n\"Test runners → Planned\" section. 232 is the standing\ntest-infrastructure issue for the project (coverage map + runner\ninventory); keeping the runner design alongside the coverage view\nmeans the next person who picks this up sees both halves at once.\n\nThe original design notes (goals, output shape, filtering, stale-\nbinary check) are preserved verbatim under 232's \"Test runners →\nPlanned — `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh`\" subsection.\n\nThe script itself has not yet been written. Tracking continues\nunder 232.",
    "originalFile":"# 316 — Simple test runner script\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`make test` builds and runs every unit-test binary plus the\nintegration runner. The output is helpful when you want to verify\nthat everything still passes at the end of a working session, but\nit's noisy when you're iterating on one specific change:\n\n- The build phase prints `→ src/foo.c`, `→ src/bar.c`, ... for\n  every file that compiles or relinks. On a clean tree that's\n  dozens of lines before the first test runs.\n- Tests are run from inside a Make recipe (a `for` loop). If one\n  binary fails, the recipe aborts and you don't see the results\n  for binaries that would have run after it.\n- The integration runner (`scripts/run-tests.sh`) is interleaved\n  with unit tests, mixing two scales of test output in one stream.\n\nThe current behavior is fine for \"ship it\" verification. It's\nsuboptimal as a development loop.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA separate script (`scripts/run-unit-tests.sh`) that runs the\nalready-built unit-test binaries one by one and reports their\nresults in a uniform format. No build step. No make. Just:\nlocate the binaries, run them in turn, capture stdout/stderr,\nprint a one-line per-binary summary, and at the end print a\ntotals line and a list of any failures.\n\nGoals:\n\n1. **Cheap to invoke.** No make recursion, no spec rebuilds,\n   no integration tests. If the build is current, the script\n   runs in well under a second.\n2. **Continues past failures.** Every test binary runs, even if\n   an earlier one fails. The summary at the bottom names what\n   went wrong.\n3. **Pretty output by default; mineable output on request.** A\n   `--quiet` mode that prints just the totals line is enough for\n   CI pre-merge gates. A `--verbose` mode dumps each binary's\n   full output. The default is per-binary one-line status.\n4. **Filterable.** A positional argument like\n   `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh 009` runs only the binaries whose\n   names start with `009`, so iterating on one slot-store change\n   doesn't require re-running every test.\n\nOut of scope: building the binaries, running integration tests\n(that's `scripts/run-tests.sh`), running specs (those are\nimplicitly tested via the binaries that depend on them).\n\n## Concept\n\nThe build system already produces `build/tests/<name>-test`\nbinaries; one per test source file under `tests/`. The script\ndiscovers them via a glob, sorts them by filename (which sorts\nby leading numeric index, which is the project's natural\nread-order), and runs each one.\n\nEach binary already prints its own header (`009-slot-store-test:`)\nand per-test status lines. The script captures the output, parses\nthe last line (`N passed, M failed`) for the per-binary verdict,\nand prints a per-binary summary like:\n\n```\n  009-slot-store-test                          16 / 16  ok\n  010-graph-loader-test                        13 / 13  ok\n  015-large-value-heap-test                     8 /  8  ok\n  ...\n```\n\nA failing binary prints its captured output below the summary\nline so the failure is visible without re-running.\n\nThe very last line is:\n\n```\n  113 / 113 tests passed (14 binaries)\n```\n\n…or, on failure:\n\n```\n  111 / 113 tests passed (14 binaries; 1 binary with failures: 009-slot-store-test)\n```\n\nExit code: zero if every binary passes; non-zero with the count\nof failing binaries otherwise.\n\n## Convention compliance\n\nPer the project's script rules (CLAUDE.md):\n\n- Hard-coded `${DIR}` at the top; first argument optionally\n  overrides it.\n- All paths under `${DIR}`.\n- Each shell command on its own line (no chained `||` /\n  `&&` pipelines for control flow; assign command output to\n  variables and branch on the variable).\n- Lives at `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh`, runnable from any cwd.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh` with the layout described\n   above.\n2. Verify it picks up every existing `build/tests/*-test`\n   binary and produces the expected totals.\n3. Verify the filter argument works: `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh\n   015` runs just the lvh test binary.\n4. Verify `--quiet` and `--verbose` modes both produce useful\n   output.\n5. Provoke a failure (modify one test temporarily) and confirm\n   the failure is reported, exit code is non-zero, and the\n   captured output is visible.\n6. Document the script in `Makefile`'s `help` target, or add a\n   `make quicktest` alias that calls it.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `scripts/run-unit-tests.sh` — new\n- `Makefile` — optional `quicktest` target\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — sibling script for integration tests;\n  this issue covers the unit-test counterpart\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should the script also verify the binaries are up to date with\n  their sources? Cheap: `stat` the binary and its `.c` and\n  complain if the source is newer. The user might prefer \"just\n  run what's built\" so they can deliberately test old binaries.\n  Default to no warning; offer a `--check-stale` flag.\n- Filter syntax: prefix-match on the test name is simple; should\n  it accept glob patterns too? Start simple. Extend if needed.\n",

{
  "isSidechain":false,

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Issue 217 — \"Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink.\" Currently in `issues/` (reopened for Part C).\n\n**Three parts, layered:**\n\n**Part A** *(shipped)* — `libs/text.lua` exposes `M.concat(sep, ...)` and `M.split(text, sep)`. `concat` is variadic so its `text` input can grow without source edits. `split` returns a Lua array; the driver shim JSON-encodes for the single output wire (multi-wire fan-out was deliberately rejected — output count isn't known at design time).\n\n**Part B** *(shipped)* — per-input variadic UI in `assets/js/004-inspector.js`. A box gets a `variadic_inputs` array of base names; slots are stored as `<base>_<index>` in `inputs`. Helpers cover the lifecycle: `make_variadic` (rename `text` → `text_0`), `unmake_variadic` (collapse back), `add_variadic_slot` (auto-grow on the last slot), `remove_variadic_slot` (delete + renumber). Schema accepts `variadic_inputs` (`src/001-schema.lua`). Auto-grow triggers on wire-connect and value-set; shrink is **only** via explicit `×` button — deliberate, so transient editing doesn't lose structure.\n\n**Part C** *(open, was blocked on 231)* — reject the `var` toggle on a non-variadic parameter. Today the toggle is user-asserted; if the underlying function doesn't accept varargs, extra positional args are silently swallowed (Lua/Bash drop trailing args; C errors or ignores). This is the silent-error class issue 230 closed off — same shape, different surface.\n\nThe fix: the inspector asks `langs/<name>/parser.js` for the function's signature when rendering a `call` box. If the port name is in the parser's `variadic_tail`-implied list, show the `var` button; otherwise hide it. The schema/validator does the same check at compile time (issue 309) so pre-existing maps get caught.\n\n**Status note worth flagging:** 217 says Part C is \"blocked on issue 231,\" but 231 has landed — `langs/lua/parser.js` and `langs/bash/parser.js` exist and export `variadic_tail` (the exact field Part C wants). The new parser tests (issue 232) guard the `variadic_tail` contract specifically because Part C will lean on it. So Part C is **unblocked** — just unimplemented. The blockers line in 217 should be updated, and the inspector + validator changes from \"Implementation steps (post-231)\" can begin.\n\nWant me to update 217's status line and start on the Part C implementation? The work is well-scoped: pass `variadic_tail` from the file-browser's on-select handler through to `mk_port_display`, gate the `var` button render, and mirror the check in `src/001-schema.lua` / `src/002-validate-map.lua`."
      }],

```json
{

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"You're right and I was rebuilding the same crystal I was supposed to break.\n\n**On 217 being stale.** Multiple axes:\n- \"Concat box\" is wrong framing — there's no special box kind, it's just `M.concat` in `libs/text.lua` invoked by any call box. The issue title and Part A still talk like there's a dedicated box.\n- \"Split returns a JSON-encoded array on the single output wire\" is also stale. That was the phase-2 transport story. Phase 3 (issue 312, same-language fast path) classifies edges and only JSON-encodes when crossing a language boundary. So `M.split` returning a Lua array is correct when the downstream box is Lua, and the runtime handles encoding when it isn't. The issue's framing predates that mechanism.\n- Honestly, `split` without a fan-out primitive is awkward on its own. The canonical pattern is `split → iterator (221)` so each part lands on its own dispatch. Outside that pairing it's just \"an array on a wire.\"\n\n**On `variadic_tail` per-function detection — yes, you're right, it doesn't work.** Let me actually re-derive why instead of waving:\n\n- Every Lua function already accepts N positional args. `function f(a)` with 5 args passed: 4 silently dropped. The `...` in the signature is the function declaring it *cares* about extras, not declaring whether the *runtime* can pass them. Same in Bash — every function gets `$@` whether it touches it or not. Same in C through the dispatch wrapper — `argc`/`argv` is the universal call shape (issue 304).\n- So \"is this function variadic\" is the wrong question. Every function in every supported language is variadic at the calling-convention level. What varies is what the function does with extras.\n- Putting that distinction in `parser.js` means the editor cracks open source files and runs language-specific regex to answer a question the runtime doesn't even care about. That's exactly the per-language ossification the language-spec model was supposed to replace.\n- And it can't extend. Adding Python means writing a Python parser. Adding Rust means writing a Rust parser. Each one has to encode that language's idea of \"variadic-ness\" in a regex.\n\n**Update on language-spec-handles-variadic: there is none.** It's in 217's \"Future development ideas\" section as a sketch, and we discussed it, but no spec field exists. No `langs/<name>/spec.c` declares a variadic shape. The parser.js work I just shipped under 231/232 went the **opposite** direction — it put per-function detection in the editor. I locked the wrong contract in with tests.\n\n**Where the right direction actually goes:**\n\nThe language spec declares its calling convention shape — that's already implicit in how `spec.c` unpacks `argc`/`argv` for the dispatch action. We make it explicit: every spec declares that it accepts N positional args and what shape the language exposes them as (Lua `...`, Bash `\"$@\"`, C `argv[]`). That declaration is one constant per spec, not per-function. The editor reads it the same way it loads the lexer — once per language.\n\nThe `var` toggle on a port then doesn't ask \"does this function accept varargs,\" it asks \"does this language support variadic at the calling convention.\" For every shipped language so far, the answer is yes. The toggle is enabled universally.\n\nIf a user wires 5 inputs to a function that internally only reads the first, that's the user's mistake — same class as wiring a string into a port the function treats as a number. The runtime doesn't police it; the editor surfaces it via documentation (the parsed signature shows `f(a)`, so the user sees the arity), not via gating.\n\nThat collapses Part C from \"block the toggle\" to \"show the signature clearly enough that the user sees what they're doing.\"\n\n**On the new tests** — `tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs` and `tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs` assert `variadic_tail` round-trips. If we drop the field from `parser.js` (which we should, since it was answering the wrong question), those assertions go with it. The remaining tests — input names, output names, declaration order, nested-block handling — are still worth keeping. Roughly half each file gets trimmed.\n\n**Concrete next moves, if you want to walk this back:**\n\n1. Add a `variadic_shape` constant to each `langs/<name>/spec.c` (positional, for all three shipped languages today).\n2. Drop `variadic_tail` from both `parser.js` files and trim those assertions from the new tests.\n3. Rewrite 217 from scratch — the concat-box framing, split's JSON story, and Part C are all wrong. The replacement is short: \"variadic is a property of the language calling convention; the spec declares it; the editor reads the spec; the `var` toggle is gated by the spec, not by source parsing.\"\n4. Update the test coverage map (232) so the parser tests' scope reflects the trimmed reality.\n\nBefore I touch any of that — does that match what you were gesturing at, or am I still missing something? I want to think with you on this rather than barrel into another wrong direction."
      }],

This file tells the *editor* the\n// language-level facts the UI needs — things that are true of\n// every function in the language, not facts about any particular\n// function's source.\n//\n// `variadic_shape` answers: how does this language accept \"extra\"\n// positional arguments at call time? \"positional\" means every\n// function can be called with N args, period — the language's\n// calling convention drops or exposes extras as it sees fit. For\n// Lua that's literally always: `function f(a)` called with five\n// args silently keeps the first and `...` would have captured the\n// rest. The fact that the *source* doesn't write `...` is the\n// function author's choice, not a runtime constraint.\n//\n// The editor reads this constant to decide whether the inspector's\n// `var` toggle is offered for ports on a Lua box. The toggle is a\n// data-model affordance for grouping N inputs onto one logical\n// port — not a guarantee that the function will use them. Mis-wire\n// is the user's call; the editor's job is to show what the source\n// declares (via parser.js) so the user can see the arity they're\n// working with.\n\nexport const LANGUAGE_SPEC = {\n  name: 'lua',\n  file_ext: '.lua',\n  variadic_shape: 'positional',\n};\n",

Whether the\n// language *accepts* extra positional args at call time is not a\n// per-function property and not the parser's job; that's declared\n// once per language in `langs/<name>/spec.js` via `variadic_shape`.\n// The function's signature still drives the displayed port names so\n// the user can see the arity the author wrote.\nexport function parse_functions(content) {\n  const fns   = [];\n  const fn_re = /^function\\s+M\\.(\\w+)\\s*\\(([^)]*)\\)/mg;\n  let m;\n  while ((m = fn_re.exec(content)) !== null) {\n    const body_start = m.index + m[0].length;\n    const body_end   = lua_fn_end(content, body_start);\n    const body       = content.slice(body_start, body_end);\n    const raw_params = m[2].trim()\n      ? m[2].split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)\n      : [];\n    const inputs  = raw_params.filter(p => p !== '...');\n    const outputs = parse_returns(body);\n    fns.push({ name: m[1], inputs, outputs });\n  }\n  return fns;\n}\n// }}}",
    "originalFile":"// langs/lua/parser.js — Lua signature parser for the editor's file\n// browser. Issue 231 moved this code out of assets/js/007-filebrowser.js\n// so per-language knowledge lives next to the rest of each language's\n// pieces (spec.c, Makefile, lexer.js).\n//\n// The contract is one ES-module export, `parse_functions(content)`,\n// returning an array of records describing every public function the\n// browser should offer. The file browser does the rest — listing,\n// click-to-pick, port population.\n\n// {{{ lua_fn_end\n// Returns the index of the closing 'end' / 'until' that matches the\n// function body starting at body_start. Tracks nesting depth by\n// counting block openers and closers. Does not attempt to skip string\n// literals — good enough for well-formatted source.\nfunction lua_fn_end(content, body_start) {\n  const tok = /\\b(function|if|while|for|repeat|do|end|until)\\b/g;\n  tok.lastIndex = body_start;\n  let depth = 1;\n  let m;\n  while ((m = tok.exec(content)) !== null) {\n    const kw = m[1];\n    if (kw === 'end' || kw === 'until') {\n      depth--;\n      if (depth === 0) return m.index;\n    } else {\n      depth++;\n    }\n  }\n  return content.length;\n}\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ parse_returns\n// Scans a function body for `return` statements; returns an array of\n// output names. Bare identifiers in the return list become port names;\n// any complex expression collapses to a single \"result\" port.\nfunction parse_returns(body) {\n  const re    = /\\breturn\\b\\s*([^\\n]+)/g;\n  const names = new Set();\n  let m;\n  while ((m = re.exec(body)) !== null) {\n    const expr = m[1].replace(/--.*$/, '').trim();\n    if (!expr) continue;\n    if (/[\"']|\\.\\./.test(expr)) { names.add('result'); continue; }\n    const parts = expr.split(',');\n    parts.forEach(part => {\n      part = part.trim();\n      if (/^[a-zA-Z_]\\w*$/.test(part) &&\n          !['nil','true','false','not','and','or','end'].includes(part)) {\n        names.add(part);\n      } else if (parts.length === 1 && part) {\n        names.add('result');\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  return [...names];\n}\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ parse_functions\n// Returns [{name, inputs, outputs, variadic_tail}] for every\n// `function M.<name>(<params>)` declared in the file.\n//\n// The `variadic_tail` field is the addition from issue 217 part C\n// (reopened): true when the parameter list ends with `...`, meaning\n// the function accepts more positional args than its declared params.\n// The trailing `...` is stripped from `inputs` so the editor's port\n// list reflects only the named parameters; the editor uses\n// `variadic_tail` to decide whether marking a port variadic is\n// actually supported by the source.\nexport function parse_functions(content) {\n  const fns   = [];\n  const fn_re = /^function\\s+M\\.(\\w+)\\s*\\(([^)]*)\\)/mg;\n  let m;\n  while ((m = fn_re.exec(content)) !== null) {\n    const body_start = m.index + m[0].length;\n    const body_end   = lua_fn_end(content, body_start);\n    const body       = content.slice(body_start, body_end);\n    const raw_params = m[2].trim()\n      ?     "originalFile":"// 232 — Tests for langs/lua/parser.js (issue 232).\n//\n// Locks in the contract `parse_functions(content)` is expected to\n// hold: it returns an ordered array of\n// `{name, inputs, outputs, variadic_tail}` records for every\n// `function M.<name>(<params>)` in the source.     "newString":"// 233 — Tests for langs/bash/parser.js (issue 232).\n//\n// Locks in `parse_functions(content)` for Bash. Single-output rule\n// (issue 218) means every function reports outputs=['output']; the\n// interesting state is on `inputs`. Whether Bash accepts extra\n// positional args at call time is a `langs/bash/spec.js` concern,\n// not per-function.\n//\n// Run from any directory:  node --test tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs",
    "originalFile":"// 233 — Tests for langs/bash/parser.js (issue 232).\n//\n// Locks in `parse_functions(content)` for Bash. Single-output rule\n// (issue 218) means every function reports outputs=['output']; the\n// interesting state is on `inputs` and `variadic_tail`.\n//\n// Run from any directory:  node --test tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\n// Override project root with SORAMECH_DIR=... when re-hosted. `node\n// --test` consumes positional args as additional test files, so the\n// project-DIR pattern uses an env var instead of argv here.\n\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport { strict as assert } from 'node:assert';\n\nconst DIR = process.env.SORAMECH_DIR || '/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech';\n\nconst { parse_functions } = await import(`${DIR}/langs/bash/parser.js`);\n\n// {{{ test('\"$@\" reference flips variadic_tail on')\ntest('\"$@\" reference flips variadic_tail on', () => {\n  const src = `\neach_arg() {\n    local prefix=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    for x in \"$@\"; do\n        printf '%s%s\\\\n' \"$prefix\" \"$x\"\n    done\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.equal(fns.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].name, 'each_arg');\n  assert.equal(fns[0].variadic_tail, true);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].outputs, ['output']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('locals named from positional params become input names')\ntest('locals named from positional params become input names', () => {\n  const src = `\nwrite_msg() {\n    local path=\"$1\"\n    local body=\"$2\"\n    printf '%s\\\\n' \"$body\" > \"$path\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.equal(fns.length, 1);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['path', 'body']);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].variadic_tail, false);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('positional refs without locals fall back to argN')\ntest('positional refs without locals fall back to argN', () => {\n  const src = `\nshout() {\n    printf '%s!' \"$1\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['arg1']);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].variadic_tail, false);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('gaps in local bindings are filled with argN placeholders')\ntest('gaps in local bindings are filled with argN placeholders', () => {\n  // Only $1 and $3 named — $2 should appear as arg2 so port order\n  // stays positional.\n  const src = `\nsparse() {\n    local first=\"$1\"\n    local third=\"$3\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['first', 'arg2', 'third']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('no positional refs at all means empty inputs')\ntest('no positional refs at all means empty inputs', () => {\n  const src = `\ngreet() {\n    echo \"hello\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, []);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].variadic_tail, false);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('control-flow keywords that look like fn decls are skipped')\ntest('control-flow keywords that look like fn decls are skipped', () => {\n  // `if() {` and `for() {` are not legal bash but the parser's\n  // regex matches `<word>() {` so the skip-set defends against\n  // false positives. Real fn after them should still show up.\n  const src = `\nreal_fn() {\n    echo ok\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.equal(fns.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].name, 'real_fn');\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('multiple functions are discovered in declaration order')\ntest('multiple functions are discovered in declaration order', () => {\n  const src = `\na() { echo 1; }\nb() { echo 2; }\nc() { echo 3; }\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns.map(f => f.name), ['a', 'b', 'c']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('braced positional ${N} forms are recognised')\ntest('braced positional ${N} forms are recognised', () => {\n  const src = `\nbraced() {\n    local first=\"\\${1}\"\n    local second=\"\\${2}\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['first', 'second']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('empty source returns empty list')\ntest('empty source returns empty list', () => {\n  assert.deepEqual(parse_functions(''), []);\n});\n// }}}\n",

    "oldString":"// {{{ test('no positional refs at all means empty inputs')\ntest('no positional refs at all means empty inputs', () => {\n  const src = `\ngreet() {\n    echo \"hello\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, []);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].variadic_tail, false);\n});\n// }}}",

    "newString":"// {{{ test('no positional refs at all means empty inputs')\ntest('no positional refs at all means empty inputs', () => {\n  const src = `\ngreet() {\n    echo \"hello\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, []);\n});\n// }}}",
    "originalFile":"// 233 — Tests for langs/bash/parser.js (issue 232).\n//\n// Locks in `parse_functions(content)` for Bash. Single-output rule\n// (issue 218) means every function reports outputs=['output']; the\n// interesting state is on `inputs`. Whether Bash accepts extra\n// positional args at call time is a `langs/bash/spec.js` concern,\n// not per-function.\n//\n// Run from any directory:  node --test tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\n// Override project root with SORAMECH_DIR=... when re-hosted. `node\n// --test` consumes positional args as additional test files, so the\n// project-DIR pattern uses an env var instead of argv here.\n\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport { strict as assert } from 'node:assert';\n\nconst DIR = process.env.SORAMECH_DIR || '/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech';\n\nconst { parse_functions } = await import(`${DIR}/langs/bash/parser.js`);\n\n// {{{ test('output is always the single port \"output\"')\ntest('output is always the single port \"output\"', () => {\n  const src = `\neach_arg() {\n    local prefix=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    for x in \"$@\"; do\n        printf '%s%s\\\\n' \"$prefix\" \"$x\"\n    done\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.equal(fns.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].name, 'each_arg');\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].outputs, ['output']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('locals named from positional params become input names')\ntest('locals named from positional params become input names', () => {\n  const src = `\nwrite_msg() {\n    local path=\"$1\"\n    local body=\"$2\"\n    printf '%s\\\\n' \"$body\" > \"$path\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.equal(fns.length, 1);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['path', 'body']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('positional refs without locals fall back to argN')\ntest('positional refs without locals fall back to argN', () => {\n  const src = `\nshout() {\n    printf '%s!' \"$1\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['arg1']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('gaps in local bindings are filled with argN placeholders')\ntest('gaps in local bindings are filled with argN placeholders', () => {\n  // Only $1 and $3 named — $2 should appear as arg2 so port order\n  // stays positional.\n  const src = `\nsparse() {\n    local first=\"$1\"\n    local third=\"$3\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['first', 'arg2', 'third']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('no positional refs at all means empty inputs')\ntest('no positional refs at all means empty inputs', () => {\n  const src = `\ngreet() {\n    echo \"hello\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, []);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].variadic_tail, false);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('control-flow keywords that look like fn decls are skipped')\ntest('control-flow keywords that look like fn decls are skipped', () => {\n  // `if() {` and `for() {` are not legal bash but the parser's\n  // regex matches `<word>() {` so the skip-set defends against\n  // false positives. Real fn after them should still show up.\n  const src = `\nreal_fn() {\n    echo ok\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.equal(fns.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(fns[0].name, 'real_fn');\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('multiple functions are discovered in declaration order')\ntest('multiple functions are discovered in declaration order', () => {\n  const src = `\na() { echo 1; }\nb() { echo 2; }\nc() { echo 3; }\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns.map(f => f.name), ['a', 'b', 'c']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('braced positional ${N} forms are recognised')\ntest('braced positional ${N} forms are recognised', () => {\n  const src = `\nbraced() {\n    local first=\"\\${1}\"\n    local second=\"\\${2}\"\n}\n`;\n  const fns = parse_functions(src);\n  assert.deepEqual(fns[0].inputs, ['first', 'second']);\n});\n// }}}\n\n// {{{ test('empty source returns empty list')\ntest('empty source returns empty list', () => {\n  assert.deepEqual(parse_functions(''), []);\n});\n// }}}\n",
