Acceptable for current fixtures; a size-class","   allocator with eager-coalesce is the upgrade path if profiling","   flags it.","+","+### Retraction of the monotonic-growth deferral — 2026-05-19","+","+The two deferrals listed immediately above this entry no longer","+reflect the design. Monotonic growth was being described as","+\"acceptable for current fixtures.\" It isn't acceptable — it's a","+memory leak by design, and any long-running workload (multi-day","+runs, anything driven by an LLM in a loop, anything that","+accumulates) will reproduce it as a real problem. Calling it","+deferred made it easier to skip; calling it a leak makes it clear","+why the skip isn't safe.","+","+The design above this implementation log has been rewritten","+accordingly. There are no longer two stores. There is one","+allocator that serves both compile-time-known sizes and","+runtime-only-known sizes from a shared pool, with reference","+counting driving deallocation, an O(1) eager neighbor-merge on","+return, and a deeper sweep on the two triggers described in the","+allocator section (\"at the moment an allocation would otherwise","+fail\" and \"at quiescence between task batches\"). Both triggers","+are deterministic — they react to the program's own behavior","+rather than to wall-clock time.","+","+What this means in terms of work remaining:","+","+- The chained-block region currently serving variable-size values","+  gets replaced by the unified allocator above. The slot-store","+  cells that hold large-value pointers stay; what they point into","+  changes from the bump-allocated chain to the size-class","+  allocator's chunks.","+- The slot store's small-fixed-size path adopts the same","+  allocator. Today that path malloc's each slot's cell-array","+  separately; under the new design every cell-array is a chunk","+  from the unified allocator.","+- The dispatch layer learns to increment and decrement reference","+  counts when it hands values from producer to consumer. This is","+  the widest change in scope — many places — but each individual","+  change is one line. The new allocator depends on these calls","+  being correct: a missed decrement leaks; a missed increment","+  frees a value that's still in use.","+- The address-ordered chunk list (described in the allocator","+  section) is added alongside the size-class lists.","+- The deeper sweep is implemented and wired into the two trigger","+  points.","+","+The implementation has not been started; this entry is the","+design commitment, not a completion notice. The earlier","+\"acceptable for current fixtures\" framing is withdrawn."]

        "type":"text",
        "text":"Tests still green (the change was design-document only; no runtime code touched yet).\n\n**What's in the file now:**\n\nThe earlier \"Lifetime\" section that flatly said there's no reference counting has been rewritten to distinguish two things that were running together — the box's slot record (still lives the whole run, as before) and the values flowing through it (now reference-counted memory chunks served by the unified allocator). That distinction was getting blurred in casual talk; the file now makes it explicit.\n\nThe \"Allocation strategy\" section has been restructured around the one-allocator idea. It now reads as one connected story: how sizes are learned from the graph before the run, the two doors for declared-size versus runtime-size allocation, reference counting as the deallocation signal, the cheap neighbor-merge on every free, and the deeper sweep on the two deterministic triggers (allocation-would-otherwise-fail, and quiescence). The address-ordered chunk list that both merge steps depend on is described after them, where it actually makes sense in the narrative.\n\nThe old \"Large-value heap (variable-size payloads)\" subsection is gone as a separate concept. Its responsibilities — handling values whose size isn't known at compile time — are now described as door 2 of the unified allocator, drawing chunks from the same memory the declared-size path uses. The \"why one allocator instead of two\" subsection explains why the earlier split was a design mistake, so a future reader who finds the implementation logs talking about two stores understands the trajectory.\n\nAt the bottom of the implementation log, a retraction entry explicitly withdraws the \"acceptable for current fixtures\" framing. It names monotonic growth as a memory leak by design, points at the rewritten sections above, and enumerates the work remaining: replace the bump-allocated variable-size pool with the unified allocator, adopt the same allocator for the small fixed-size path, wire reference counting through the dispatch layer, add the address-ordered chunk list, implement the deeper sweep. It states clearly that this is a design commitment, not a completion notice — the allocator hasn't been built yet, but the design isn't deferred anymore.\n\n**On the two questions you asked, recorded in the file:**\n\nThe \"how does the loader know sizes\" answer lives in the new \"How the allocator learns sizes ahead of time\" subsection. Short version of what's in the file: known sizes come from each box's output-size declaration in the graph metadata, deduplicated into size classes pre-warmed before the run. Unknown sizes are declared as \"size unknown\" by the box; the loader doesn't pre-warm a list for them, and they go through door 2 at runtime.\n\nThe deterministic-sweep answer lives in the \"When does the bigger sweep run\" subsection. The mandatory trigger is the moment an allocation would otherwise fail. The opportunistic trigger is quiescence between task batches. The threshold-based trigger is mentioned as a third option and rejected for now (works, but needs tuning, and the first two cover the same ground without it)."

The design in the file covers a new allocator module, replacing one existing module, modifying another, and wiring reference counting through a third. That's bigger than one focused session.\n\nThe responsible sequence:\n\n1. **Build the new allocator as a standalone module, with its own tests.** Doesn't touch any existing systems. Verifiable in isolation.\n2. **Switch the variable-size-payload path to use it.** Removes the current bump-allocated chain that's the memory leak. Existing tests at the slot-store boundary should pass unchanged.\n3. **Switch the fixed-size value path to use it too.** Currently the slot store calls plain malloc per slot at startup. You'll see the new allocator with its full test surface; the existing system keeps running unchanged. After you've looked at it we can decide on the rest."

          "content":"/* src/016-unified-allocator.c — implementation of the unified\n * allocator declared in 016-unified-allocator.h.\n *\n * The story this file tells, in order:\n *\n *   A chunk header carries the chunk's size, refcount, free flag,\n *   and three pointers: two for the address-ordered doubly-linked\n *   list (so neighbor-merge can find what's physically next to it),\n *   and one for the free-list it currently sits on (when free).\n *   The payload bytes follow the header as a flexible array.\n *\n *   The allocator owns a sorted array of size classes. For each\n *   class there's a head pointer into a singly-linked free-list of\n *   chunks of exactly that size.\n *\n *   The allocator also owns a list of \"regions\" — single mallocs\n *   from the OS, each carved into chunks at creation time. Every\n *   chunk in a region is in the region's own address-ordered list\n *   (so the prev/next pointers actually reflect physical\n *   adjacency). Region boundaries are non-mergeable.\n *\n *   ua_alloc(size) finds the smallest class whose size >= request,\n *   pops the head of that class's free-list, marks the chunk\n *   allocated (refcount=1, is_free=0), and returns it.\n *\n *   If the class is empty, the allocator tries larger classes.\n *   If every class is empty, the allocator runs the sweep, then\n *   tries again. If still nothing, it grows the heap by allocating\n *   a new region containing one chunk of the requested size (with\n *   the request rounded up to the requested class size if it\n *   matched a declared class, or aligned up if it didn't).\n *\n *   ua_unref drops the refcount. When it reaches zero, the chunk\n *   is pushed onto its class's free-list, then the deallocator\n *   checks the chunk's addr_prev and addr_next. If either neighbor\n *   is free, the two chunks are unlinked from their current\n *   free-lists, fused (the lower chunk's size absorbs the higher\n *   chunk; the higher chunk's address-list slot is removed), and\n *   the merged chunk is pushed onto the appropriate free-list. The\n *   merged size might match an existing class (push onto that\n *   class's list) or it might not (push onto the smallest class\n *   whose size >= merged_size, which is acceptable because alloc\n *   only ever looks at the chunk's actual size, not its class).\n *\n * One mutex on the whole allocator. Per-class locking is the\n * documented next step but not in this stage.\n *\n * Designed in issue 302's rewrite (2026-05-19).\n */\n\n#include \"016-unified-allocator.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Alignment */\n/* Payload alignment — 16 bytes is sufficient for any standard C\n * scalar or SIMD vector. Chunk headers are sized so the flexible\n * array begins on this boundary. */\n#define UA_ALIGN 16u\n\nstatic inline size_t align_up(size_t n, size_t a)\n{\n    return (n + (a - 1u)) & ~(a - 1u);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Chunk header */\nstruct ua_chunk {\n    /* Address-ordered doubly-linked list, scoped to the chunk's\n     * region. NULL at region boundaries — never link across regions. */\n    struct ua_chunk *addr_prev;\n    struct ua_chunk *addr_next;\n\n    /* Singly-linked free-list pointer. Only meaningful when\n     * is_free == 1. */\n    struct ua_chunk *free_next;\n\n    /* Bytes available to the caller (does not count this header). */\n    size_t size;\n\n    /* The class this chunk's free-list belongs to. Set at chunk\n     * creation; updated when an eager merge promotes the chunk to\n     * a different list. */\n    size_t class_size;\n\n    /* Reference count. Atomic for ua_ref/ua_unref under non-locked\n     * paths in future stages; mutex covers the structural operations\n     * (free-list manipulation, neighbor merging) where atomicity of\n     * the count alone is not sufficient. */\n    _Atomic uint32_t refcount;\n\n    uint8_t is_free;\n    uint8_t _pad[7];\n\n    /* Flexible-array payload. Header is sized so this begins on a\n     * UA_ALIGN boundary on every platform we target. */\n    uint8_t data[];\n};\n\n#define UA_HEADER_BYTES sizeof(struct ua_chunk)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Heap struct */\nstruct ua {\n    pthread_mutex_t mu;\n\n    /* Size classes, sorted ascending. */\n    size_t       *class_sizes;\n    ua_chunk_t  **class_heads;     /* free-list head per class */\n    size_t        n_classes;\n    size_t        classes_cap;\n\n    /* Regions. Each entry is the base pointer of one big malloc. */\n    void        **regions;\n    ua_chunk_t  **region_firsts;   /* first chunk in each region */\n    size_t        n_regions;\n    size_t        regions_cap;\n\n    /* Stats. */\n    _Atomic uint64_t bytes_in_use;\n    _Atomic uint64_t bytes_free;\n    _Atomic uint64_t bytes_total;\n    _Atomic uint32_t alloc_calls;\n    _Atomic uint32_t free_calls;\n    _Atomic uint32_t neighbor_merges;\n    _Atomic uint32_t sweep_merges;\n    _Atomic uint32_t grow_calls;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — find_class_index */\n/* Smallest class index whose class_sizes[i] >= want. Returns\n * h->n_classes if none. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic size_t find_class_index(const ua_t *h, size_t want)\n{\n    /* Linear scan: class counts are tiny in practice (the graph\n     * declares a handful of distinct sizes). Binary search becomes\n     * worthwhile only past a few dozen classes; not the case here. */\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_classes; i++) {\n        if (h->class_sizes[i] >= want) return i;\n    }\n    return h->n_classes;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — ensure_class */\n/* Make sure a class with this exact size exists; return its index.\n * If the class is new, the new free-list head is NULL. Caller\n * holds h->mu. Returns SIZE_MAX on allocation failure. */\nstatic size_t ensure_class(ua_t *h, size_t size)\n{\n    /* Already present? */\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_classes; i++) {\n        if (h->class_sizes[i] == size) return i;\n    }\n\n    /* Grow the arrays if needed. */\n    if (h->n_classes == h->classes_cap) {\n        size_t new_cap = h->classes_cap ? h->classes_cap * 2 : 8;\n        size_t      *new_sizes = realloc(h->class_sizes, new_cap * sizeof *new_sizes);\n        if (!new_sizes) return (size_t)-1;\n        h->class_sizes = new_sizes;\n        ua_chunk_t **new_heads = realloc(h->class_heads, new_cap * sizeof *new_heads);\n        if (!new_heads) return (size_t)-1;\n        h->class_heads = new_heads;\n        h->classes_cap = new_cap;\n    }\n\n    /* Insert sorted. */\n    size_t pos = h->n_classes;\n    while (pos > 0 && h->class_sizes[pos - 1] > size) pos--;\n    if (pos < h->n_classes) {\n        memmove(&h->class_sizes[pos + 1], &h->class_sizes[pos],\n                (h->n_classes - pos) * sizeof *h->class_sizes);\n        memmove(&h->class_heads[pos + 1], &h->class_heads[pos],\n                (h->n_classes - pos) * sizeof *h->class_heads);\n    }\n    h->class_sizes[pos] = size;\n    h->class_heads[pos] = NULL;\n    h->n_classes++;\n    return pos;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — push_to_free_list */\n/* Push `c` onto the free-list for `class_idx`. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic void push_to_free_list(ua_t *h, size_t class_idx, ua_chunk_t *c)\n{\n    c->is_free    = 1;\n    c->class_size = h->class_sizes[class_idx];\n    c->free_next  = h->class_heads[class_idx];\n    h->class_heads[class_idx] = c;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — remove_from_free_list */\n/* Unlink `c` from its current free-list. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic void remove_from_free_list(ua_t *h, ua_chunk_t *c)\n{\n    size_t idx = (size_t)-1;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_classes; i++) {\n        if (h->class_sizes[i] == c->class_size) {\n            idx = i;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if (idx == (size_t)-1) return;  /* shouldn't happen but defensive */\n\n    ua_chunk_t **link = &h->class_heads[idx];\n    while (*link && *link != c) link = &(*link)->free_next;\n    if (*link == c) *link = c->free_next;\n    c->free_next = NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — register_region */\n/* Append `base` and `first` to the region tracking arrays. Caller\n * holds h->mu. Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation failure. */\nstatic int register_region(ua_t *h, void *base, ua_chunk_t *first)\n{\n    if (h->n_regions == h->regions_cap) {\n        size_t new_cap = h->regions_cap ? h->regions_cap * 2 : 4;\n        void       **nr = realloc(h->regions,        new_cap * sizeof *nr);\n        if (!nr) return -1;\n        h->regions      = nr;\n        ua_chunk_t **nf = realloc(h->region_firsts,  new_cap * sizeof *nf);\n        if (!nf) return -1;\n        h->region_firsts = nf;\n        h->regions_cap   = new_cap;\n    }\n    h->regions[h->n_regions]       = base;\n    h->region_firsts[h->n_regions] = first;\n    h->n_regions++;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — carve_region */\n/* Build a region containing chunks per the given (size, count)\n * pairs, in declaration order. Pushes every chunk onto its class's\n * free-list and links them in address order. Caller holds h->mu.\n *\n * Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation failure. */\nstatic int carve_region(ua_t *h,\n                        const ua_class_decl_t *classes,\n                        size_t n_classes)\n{\n    size_t total = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n        size_t s = align_up(classes[i].size, UA_ALIGN);\n        total += (UA_HEADER_BYTES + s) * classes[i].prewarm_count;\n    }\n    if (total == 0) return 0;\n\n    /* One malloc, generously aligned. */\n    void *base = aligned_alloc(UA_ALIGN, align_up(total, UA_ALIGN));\n    if (!base) return -1;\n\n    /* Carve chunks back-to-back. */\n    uint8_t    *cursor = base;\n    ua_chunk_t *first  = NULL;\n    ua_chunk_t *prev   = NULL;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n        size_t s = align_up(classes[i].size, UA_ALIGN);\n        size_t class_idx = ensure_class(h, s);\n        if (class_idx == (size_t)-1) {\n            free(base);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (uint32_t k = 0; k < classes[i].prewarm_count; k++) {\n            ua_chunk_t *c = (ua_chunk_t *)cursor;\n            c->addr_prev = prev;\n            c->addr_next = NULL;\n            c->free_next = NULL;\n            c->size      = s;\n            atomic_store_explicit(&c->refcount, 0, memory_order_relaxed);\n            if (prev) prev->addr_next = c;\n            if (!first) first = c;\n            push_to_free_list(h, class_idx, c);\n            prev = c;\n            cursor += UA_HEADER_BYTES + s;\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->bytes_free, (uint64_t)s,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (register_region(h, base, first) < 0) {\n        free(base);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->bytes_total, (uint64_t)total,\n                              memory_order_relaxed);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ua_create */\nua_t *ua_create(const ua_class_decl_t *classes, size_t n_classes)\n{\n    /* Validate. */\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n        if (classes[i].size == 0) return NULL;\n    }\n\n    ua_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    if (!h) return NULL;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&h->mu, NULL) != 0) {\n        free(h);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    /* De-duplicate by summing counts for identical sizes. */\n    if (n_classes > 0) {\n        ua_class_decl_t *dedup = calloc(n_classes, sizeof *dedup);\n        if (!dedup) {\n            pthread_mutex_destroy(&h->mu);\n            free(h);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n        size_t k = 0;\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n            size_t aligned = align_up(classes[i].size, UA_ALIGN);\n            size_t j;\n            for (j = 0; j < k; j++) {\n                if (dedup[j].size == aligned) {\n                    dedup[j].prewarm_count += classes[i].prewarm_count;\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if (j == k) {\n                dedup[k].size = aligned;\n                dedup[k].prewarm_count = classes[i].prewarm_count;\n                k++;\n            }\n        }\n        if (carve_region(h, dedup, k) < 0) {\n            free(dedup);\n            ua_destroy(h);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n        free(dedup);\n    }\n\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ua_destroy */\nvoid ua_destroy(ua_t *h)\n{\n    if (!h) return;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_regions; i++) free(h->regions[i]);\n    free(h->regions);\n    free(h->region_firsts);\n    free(h->class_sizes);\n    free(h->class_heads);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&h->mu);\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — grow_for_size */\n/* Add a new region containing one chunk that satisfies `want_size`.\n * The chunk is left on the free-list of the appropriate class.\n * Caller holds h->mu. Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation\n * failure. */\nstatic int grow_for_size(ua_t *h, size_t want_size)\n{\n    size_t s = align_up(want_size, UA_ALIGN);\n    ua_class_decl_t one = { .size = s, .prewarm_count = 1 };\n    int rc = carve_region(h, &one, 1);\n    if (rc == 0) {\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->grow_calls, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — eager_merge */\n/* If either neighbor of `c` (which has just been pushed onto its\n * free-list) is free, fuse them into one larger chunk. Updates\n * stats. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic void eager_merge(ua_t *h, ua_chunk_t *c)\n{\n    /* Walk forward first: while addr_next is free, absorb it. */\n    while (c->addr_next && c->addr_next->is_free) {\n        ua_chunk_t *n = c->addr_next;\n\n        remove_from_free_list(h, c);\n        remove_from_free_list(h, n);\n\n        /* Fuse: c grows to cover the header + payload of n. */\n        c->size += UA_HEADER_BYTES + n->size;\n        c->addr_next = n->addr_next;\n        if (n->addr_next) n->addr_next->addr_prev = c;\n\n        size_t new_class = ensure_class(h, c->size);\n        if (new_class == (size_t)-1) {\n            /* Couldn't grow class array. Restore c onto a list that\n             * already exists — find any class with size matching or\n             * larger and put c there. Should never happen in practice. */\n            push_to_free_list(h, 0, c);\n            return;\n        }\n        push_to_free_list(h, new_class, c);\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->neighbor_merges, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n\n    /* Then walk backward: while addr_prev is free, prev absorbs c. */\n    while (c->addr_prev && c->addr_prev->is_free) {\n        ua_chunk_t *p = c->addr_prev;\n\n        remove_from_free_list(h, c);\n        remove_from_free_list(h, p);\n\n        p->size += UA_HEADER_BYTES + c->size;\n        p->addr_next = c->addr_next;\n        if (c->addr_next) c->addr_next->addr_prev = p;\n\n        size_t new_class = ensure_class(h, p->size);\n        if (new_class == (size_t)-1) {\n            push_to_free_list(h, 0, p);\n            return;\n        }\n        push_to_free_list(h, new_class, p);\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->neighbor_merges, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n        c = p;  /* continue from the merged chunk */\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ua_alloc */\nua_chunk_t *ua_alloc(ua_t *h, size_t size)\n{\n    if (!h || size == 0) return NULL;\n    size_t aligned = align_up(size, UA_ALIGN);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&h->mu);\n\n    for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {\n        size_t idx = find_class_index(h, aligned);\n        if (idx < h->n_classes && h->class_heads[idx]) {\n            ua_chunk_t *c = h->class_heads[idx];\n            h->class_heads[idx] = c->free_next;\n            c->free_next = NULL;\n            c->is_free   = 0;\n            atomic_store_explicit(&c->refcount, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->alloc_calls, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->bytes_in_use, (uint64_t)c->size,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&h->bytes_free, (uint64_t)c->size,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n            return c;\n        }\n        /* Try larger classes. */\n        size_t larger = idx + 1;\n        while (larger < h->n_classes && !h->class_heads[larger]) larger++;\n        if (larger < h->n_classes) {\n            ua_chunk_t *c = h->class_heads[larger];\n            h->class_heads[larger] = c->free_next;\n            c->free_next = NULL;\n            c->is_free   = 0;\n            atomic_store_explicit(&c->refcount, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->alloc_calls, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->bytes_in_use, (uint64_t)c->size,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&h->bytes_free, (uint64_t)c->size,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n            return c;\n        }\n\n        if (attempt == 0) {\n            /* Mandatory sweep before growing. */\n            uint32_t merges = 0;\n            for (size_t r = 0; r < h->n_regions; r++) {\n                ua_chunk_t *cur = h->region_firsts[r];\n                while (cur && cur->addr_next) {\n                    if (cur->is_free && cur->addr_next->is_free) {\n                        ua_chunk_t *n = cur->addr_next;\n                        remove_from_free_list(h, cur);\n                        remove_from_free_list(h, n);\n                        cur->size += UA_HEADER_BYTES + n->size;\n                        cur->addr_next = n->addr_next;\n                        if (n->addr_next) n->addr_next->addr_prev = cur;\n                        size_t new_class = ensure_class(h, cur->size);\n                        if (new_class != (size_t)-1) {\n                            push_to_free_list(h, new_class, cur);\n                        }\n                        merges++;\n                        continue;  /* re-check from cur — might fuse further */\n                    }\n                    cur = cur->addr_next;\n                }\n            }\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->sweep_merges, merges, memory_order_relaxed);\n            continue;  /* retry from the top */\n        }\n\n        if (attempt == 1) {\n            /* Grow. */\n            if (grow_for_size(h, aligned) < 0) {\n                pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n                return NULL;\n            }\n            continue;  /* retry from the top — should succeed now */\n        }\n    }\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ua_ref */\nua_chunk_t *ua_ref(ua_chunk_t *chunk)\n{\n    if (!chunk) return NULL;\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&chunk->refcount, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n    return chunk;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ua_unref */\nvoid ua_unref(ua_t *h, ua_chunk_t *chunk)\n{\n    if (!h || !chunk) return;\n    uint32_t prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&chunk->refcount, 1u,\n                                              memory_order_acq_rel);\n    if (prev != 1) return;  /* still has references */\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&h->mu);\n\n    /* It is possible (under future per-class locking) that another\n     * thread ref'd between the atomic decrement and acquiring the\n     * mutex. r < h->n_regions; r++) {\n        ua_chunk_t *cur = h->region_firsts[r];\n        while (cur && cur->addr_next) {\n            if (cur->is_free && cur->addr_next->is_free) {\n                ua_chunk_t *n = cur->addr_next;\n                remove_from_free_list(h, cur);\n                remove_from_free_list(h, n);\n                cur->size += UA_HEADER_BYTES + n->size;\n                cur->addr_next = n->addr_next;\n                if (n->addr_next) n->addr_next->addr_prev = cur;\n                size_t new_class = ensure_class(h, cur->size);\n                if (new_class != (size_t)-1) {\n                    push_to_free_list(h, new_class, cur);\n                }\n                merges++;\n                continue;\n            }\n            cur = cur->addr_next;\n        }\n    }\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->sweep_merges, merges, memory_order_relaxed);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n    return merges;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Stats accessors */\nuint64_t ua_bytes_in_use(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->bytes_in_use, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint64_t ua_bytes_free(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->bytes_free, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint64_t ua_bytes_total(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->bytes_total, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_region_count(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? (uint32_t)h->n_regions : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_alloc_calls(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->alloc_calls, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_free_calls(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->free_calls, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_neighbor_merges(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->neighbor_merges, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_sweep_merges(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->sweep_merges, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_grow_calls(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->grow_calls, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_class_free_count(const ua_t *h, size_t size)\n{\n    if (!h) return 0;\n    size_t target = align_up(size, UA_ALIGN);\n    uint32_t count = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_lock((pthread_mutex_t *)&h->mu);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_classes; i++) {\n        if (h->class_sizes[i] != target) continue;\n        for (ua_chunk_t *c = h->class_heads[i]; c; c = c->free_next) count++;\n        break;\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock((pthread_mutex_t *)&h->mu);\n    return count;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "content":"/* src/016-unified-allocator.c — implementation of the unified\n * allocator declared in 016-unified-allocator.h.\n *\n * The story this file tells, in order:\n *\n *   A chunk header carries the chunk's size, refcount, free flag,\n *   and three pointers: two for the address-ordered doubly-linked\n *   list (so neighbor-merge can find what's physically next to it),\n *   and one for the free-list it currently sits on (when free).\n *   The payload bytes follow the header as a flexible array.\n *\n *   The allocator owns a sorted array of size classes. For each\n *   class there's a head pointer into a singly-linked free-list of\n *   chunks of exactly that size.\n *\n *   The allocator also owns a list of \"regions\" — single mallocs\n *   from the OS, each carved into chunks at creation time. Every\n *   chunk in a region is in the region's own address-ordered list\n *   (so the prev/next pointers actually reflect physical\n *   adjacency). Region boundaries are non-mergeable.\n *\n *   ua_alloc(size) finds the smallest class whose size >= request,\n *   pops the head of that class's free-list, marks the chunk\n *   allocated (refcount=1, is_free=0), and returns it.\n *\n *   If the class is empty, the allocator tries larger classes.\n *   If every class is empty, the allocator runs the sweep, then\n *   tries again. When it reaches zero, the chunk\n *   is pushed onto its class's free-list, then the deallocator\n *   checks the chunk's addr_prev and addr_next. If either neighbor\n *   is free, the two chunks are unlinked from their current\n *   free-lists, fused (the lower chunk's size absorbs the higher\n *   chunk; the higher chunk's address-list slot is removed), and\n *   the merged chunk is pushed onto the appropriate free-list. The\n *   merged size might match an existing class (push onto that\n *   class's list) or it might not (push onto the smallest class\n *   whose size >= merged_size, which is acceptable because alloc\n *   only ever looks at the chunk's actual size, not its class).\n *\n * One mutex on the whole allocator. Per-class locking is the\n * documented next step but not in this stage.\n *\n * Designed in issue 302's rewrite (2026-05-19).\n */\n\n#include \"016-unified-allocator.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Alignment */\n/* Payload alignment — 16 bytes is sufficient for any standard C\n * scalar or SIMD vector. Chunk headers are sized so the flexible\n * array begins on this boundary. */\n#define UA_ALIGN 16u\n\nstatic inline size_t align_up(size_t n, size_t a)\n{\n    return (n + (a - 1u)) & ~(a - 1u);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Chunk header */\nstruct ua_chunk {\n    /* Address-ordered doubly-linked list, scoped to the chunk's\n     * region. NULL at region boundaries — never link across regions. */\n    struct ua_chunk *addr_prev;\n    struct ua_chunk *addr_next;\n\n    /* Singly-linked free-list pointer. Only meaningful when\n     * is_free == 1. */\n    struct ua_chunk *free_next;\n\n    /* Bytes available to the caller (does not count this header). */\n    size_t size;\n\n    /* The class this chunk's free-list belongs to. Set at chunk\n     * creation; updated when an eager merge promotes the chunk to\n     * a different list. */\n    size_t class_size;\n\n    /* Reference count. Atomic for ua_ref/ua_unref under non-locked\n     * paths in future stages; mutex covers the structural operations\n     * (free-list manipulation, neighbor merging) where atomicity of\n     * the count alone is not sufficient. */\n    _Atomic uint32_t refcount;\n\n    uint8_t is_free;\n    uint8_t _pad[7];\n\n    /* Flexible-array payload. Header is sized so this begins on a\n     * UA_ALIGN boundary on every platform we target. */\n    uint8_t data[];\n};\n\n#define UA_HEADER_BYTES sizeof(struct ua_chunk)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Heap struct */\nstruct ua {\n    pthread_mutex_t mu;\n\n    /* Size classes, sorted ascending. */\n    size_t       *class_sizes;\n    ua_chunk_t  **class_heads;     /* free-list head per class */\n    size_t        n_classes;\n    size_t        classes_cap;\n\n    /* Regions. Each entry is the base pointer of one big malloc. */\n    void        **regions;\n    ua_chunk_t  **region_firsts;   /* first chunk in each region */\n    size_t        n_regions;\n    size_t        regions_cap;\n\n    /* Stats. */\n    _Atomic uint64_t bytes_in_use;\n    _Atomic uint64_t bytes_free;\n    _Atomic uint64_t bytes_total;\n    _Atomic uint32_t alloc_calls;\n    _Atomic uint32_t free_calls;\n    _Atomic uint32_t neighbor_merges;\n    _Atomic uint32_t sweep_merges;\n    _Atomic uint32_t grow_calls;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — find_class_index */\n/* Smallest class index whose class_sizes[i] >= want. Returns\n * h->n_classes if none. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic size_t find_class_index(const ua_t *h, size_t want)\n{\n    /* Linear scan: class counts are tiny in practice (the graph\n     * declares a handful of distinct sizes). Binary search becomes\n     * worthwhile only past a few dozen classes; not the case here. */\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_classes; i++) {\n        if (h->class_sizes[i] >= want) return i;\n    }\n    return h->n_classes;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — ensure_class */\n/* Make sure a class with this exact size exists; return its index.\n * If the class is new, the new free-list head is NULL. Caller\n * holds h->mu. Returns SIZE_MAX on allocation failure. */\nstatic size_t ensure_class(ua_t *h, size_t size)\n{\n    /* Already present? */\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_classes; i++) {\n        if (h->class_sizes[i] == size) return i;\n    }\n\n    /* Grow the arrays if needed. */\n    if (h->n_classes == h->classes_cap) {\n        size_t new_cap = h->classes_cap ? h->classes_cap * 2 : 8;\n        size_t      *new_sizes = realloc(h->class_sizes, new_cap * sizeof *new_sizes);\n        if (!new_sizes) return (size_t)-1;\n        h->class_sizes = new_sizes;\n        ua_chunk_t **new_heads = realloc(h->class_heads, new_cap * sizeof *new_heads);\n        if (!new_heads) return (size_t)-1;\n        h->class_heads = new_heads;\n        h->classes_cap = new_cap;\n    }\n\n    /* Insert sorted. */\n    size_t pos = h->n_classes;\n    while (pos > 0 && h->class_sizes[pos - 1] > size) pos--;\n    if (pos < h->n_classes) {\n        memmove(&h->class_sizes[pos + 1], &h->class_sizes[pos],\n                (h->n_classes - pos) * sizeof *h->class_sizes);\n        memmove(&h->class_heads[pos + 1], &h->class_heads[pos],\n                (h->n_classes - pos) * sizeof *h->class_heads);\n    }\n    h->class_sizes[pos] = size;\n    h->class_heads[pos] = NULL;\n    h->n_classes++;\n    return pos;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — push_to_free_list */\n/* Push `c` onto the free-list for `class_idx`. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic void push_to_free_list(ua_t *h, size_t class_idx, ua_chunk_t *c)\n{\n    c->is_free    = 1;\n    c->class_size = h->class_sizes[class_idx];\n    c->free_next  = h->class_heads[class_idx];\n    h->class_heads[class_idx] = c;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — remove_from_free_list */\n/* Unlink `c` from its current free-list. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic void remove_from_free_list(ua_t *h, ua_chunk_t *c)\n{\n    size_t idx = (size_t)-1;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_classes; i++) {\n        if (h->class_sizes[i] == c->class_size) {\n            idx = i;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if (idx == (size_t)-1) return;  /* shouldn't happen but defensive */\n\n    ua_chunk_t **link = &h->class_heads[idx];\n    while (*link && *link != c) link = &(*link)->free_next;\n    if (*link == c) *link = c->free_next;\n    c->free_next = NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — register_region */\n/* Append `base` and `first` to the region tracking arrays. Caller\n * holds h->mu. Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation failure. */\nstatic int register_region(ua_t *h, void *base, ua_chunk_t *first)\n{\n    if (h->n_regions == h->regions_cap) {\n        size_t new_cap = h->regions_cap ? h->regions_cap * 2 : 4;\n        void       **nr = realloc(h->regions,        new_cap * sizeof *nr);\n        if (!nr) return -1;\n        h->regions      = nr;\n        ua_chunk_t **nf = realloc(h->region_firsts,  new_cap * sizeof *nf);\n        if (!nf) return -1;\n        h->region_firsts = nf;\n        h->regions_cap   = new_cap;\n    }\n    h->regions[h->n_regions]       = base;\n    h->region_firsts[h->n_regions] = first;\n    h->n_regions++;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — carve_region */\n/* Build a region containing chunks per the given (size, count)\n * pairs, in declaration order. Pushes every chunk onto its class's\n * free-list and links them in address order. Caller holds h->mu.\n *\n * Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation failure. */\nstatic int carve_region(ua_t *h,\n                        const ua_class_decl_t *classes,\n                        size_t n_classes)\n{\n    size_t total = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n        size_t s = align_up(classes[i].size, UA_ALIGN);\n        total += (UA_HEADER_BYTES + s) * classes[i].prewarm_count;\n    }\n    if (total == 0) return 0;\n\n    /* One malloc, generously aligned. */\n    void *base = aligned_alloc(UA_ALIGN, align_up(total, UA_ALIGN));\n    if (!base) return -1;\n\n    /* Carve chunks back-to-back. */\n    uint8_t    *cursor = base;\n    ua_chunk_t *first  = NULL;\n    ua_chunk_t *prev   = NULL;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n        size_t s = align_up(classes[i].size, UA_ALIGN);\n        size_t class_idx = ensure_class(h, s);\n        if (class_idx == (size_t)-1) {\n            free(base);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (uint32_t k = 0; k < classes[i].prewarm_count; k++) {\n            ua_chunk_t *c = (ua_chunk_t *)cursor;\n            c->addr_prev = prev;\n            c->addr_next = NULL;\n            c->free_next = NULL;\n            c->size      = s;\n            atomic_store_explicit(&c->refcount, 0, memory_order_relaxed);\n            if (prev) prev->addr_next = c;\n            if (!first) first = c;\n            push_to_free_list(h, class_idx, c);\n            prev = c;\n            cursor += UA_HEADER_BYTES + s;\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->bytes_free, (uint64_t)s,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (register_region(h, base, first) < 0) {\n        free(base);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->bytes_total, (uint64_t)total,\n                              memory_order_relaxed);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ua_create */\nua_t *ua_create(const ua_class_decl_t *classes, size_t n_classes)\n{\n    /* Validate. */\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n        if (classes[i].size == 0) return NULL;\n    }\n\n    ua_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    if (!h) return NULL;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&h->mu, NULL) != 0) {\n        free(h);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    /* De-duplicate by summing counts for identical sizes. */\n    if (n_classes > 0) {\n        ua_class_decl_t *dedup = calloc(n_classes, sizeof *dedup);\n        if (!dedup) {\n            pthread_mutex_destroy(&h->mu);\n            free(h);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n        size_t k = 0;\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < n_classes; i++) {\n            size_t aligned = align_up(classes[i].size, UA_ALIGN);\n            size_t j;\n            for (j = 0; j < k; j++) {\n                if (dedup[j].size == aligned) {\n                    dedup[j].prewarm_count += classes[i].prewarm_count;\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if (j == k) {\n                dedup[k].size = aligned;\n                dedup[k].prewarm_count = classes[i].prewarm_count;\n                k++;\n            }\n        }\n        if (carve_region(h, dedup, k) < 0) {\n            free(dedup);\n            ua_destroy(h);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n        free(dedup);\n    }\n\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ua_destroy */\nvoid ua_destroy(ua_t *h)\n{\n    if (!h) return;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < h->n_regions; i++) free(h->regions[i]);\n    free(h->regions);\n    free(h->region_firsts);\n    free(h->class_sizes);\n    free(h->class_heads);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&h->mu);\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — grow_for_size */\n/* Add a new region containing one chunk that satisfies `want_size`.\n * The chunk is left on the free-list of the appropriate class.\n * Caller holds h->mu. Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation\n * failure. */\nstatic int grow_for_size(ua_t *h, size_t want_size)\n{\n    size_t s = align_up(want_size, UA_ALIGN);\n    ua_class_decl_t one = { .size = s, .prewarm_count = 1 };\n    int rc = carve_region(h, &one, 1);\n    if (rc == 0) {\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->grow_calls, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — eager_merge */\n/* If either neighbor of `c` (which has just been pushed onto its\n * free-list) is free, fuse them into one larger chunk. Caller holds h->mu. */\nstatic void eager_merge(ua_t *h, ua_chunk_t *c)\n{\n    /* Walk forward first: while addr_next is free, absorb it. */\n    while (c->addr_next && c->addr_next->is_free) {\n        ua_chunk_t *n = c->addr_next;\n\n        remove_from_free_list(h, c);\n        remove_from_free_list(h, n);\n\n        /* Fuse: c grows to cover the header + payload of n. */\n        c->size += UA_HEADER_BYTES + n->size;\n        c->addr_next = n->addr_next;\n        if (n->addr_next) n->addr_next->addr_prev = c;\n\n        size_t new_class = ensure_class(h, c->size);\n        if (new_class == (size_t)-1) {\n            /* Couldn't grow class array. Should never happen in practice. */\n            push_to_free_list(h, 0, c);\n            return;\n        }\n        push_to_free_list(h, new_class, c);\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->neighbor_merges, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n\n    /* Then walk backward: while addr_prev is free, prev absorbs c. */\n    while (c->addr_prev && c->addr_prev->is_free) {\n        ua_chunk_t *p = c->addr_prev;\n\n        remove_from_free_list(h, c);\n        remove_from_free_list(h, p);\n\n        p->size += UA_HEADER_BYTES + c->size;\n        p->addr_next = c->addr_next;\n        if (c->addr_next) c->addr_next->addr_prev = p;\n\n        size_t new_class = ensure_class(h, p->size);\n        if (new_class == (size_t)-1) {\n            push_to_free_list(h, 0, p);\n            return;\n        }\n        push_to_free_list(h, new_class, p);\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->neighbor_merges, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);\n        c = p;  /* re-check from cur — might fuse further */\n                    }\n                    cur = cur->addr_next;\n                }\n            }\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->sweep_merges, merges, memory_order_relaxed);\n            continue; r < h->n_regions; r++) {\n        ua_chunk_t *cur = h->region_firsts[r];\n        while (cur && cur->addr_next) {\n            if (cur->is_free && cur->addr_next->is_free) {\n                ua_chunk_t *n = cur->addr_next;\n                remove_from_free_list(h, cur);\n                remove_from_free_list(h, n);\n                cur->size += UA_HEADER_BYTES + n->size;\n                cur->addr_next = n->addr_next;\n                if (n->addr_next) n->addr_next->addr_prev = cur;\n                size_t new_class = ensure_class(h, cur->size);\n                if (new_class != (size_t)-1) {\n                    push_to_free_list(h, new_class, cur);\n                }\n                merges++;\n                continue;\n            }\n            cur = cur->addr_next;\n        }\n    }\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&h->sweep_merges, merges, memory_order_relaxed);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&h->mu);\n    return merges;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Stats accessors */\nuint64_t ua_bytes_in_use(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->bytes_in_use, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint64_t ua_bytes_free(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->bytes_free, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint64_t ua_bytes_total(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ? atomic_load_explicit(&h->bytes_total, memory_order_relaxed) : 0;\n}\nuint32_t ua_region_count(const ua_t *h)\n{\n    return h ?           "content":"/* tests/016-unified-allocator-test.c — exercises the unified\n * allocator's contract end-to-end. Each test is independent (its\n * own heap), so failures isolate cleanly.\n *\n * What's covered:\n *   - empty-heap create/destroy round-trip\n *   - pre-warming: declared sizes produce ready-to-pop chunks\n *   - alloc + unref reuses chunks (no growth)\n *   - reference counting: extra ref keeps chunk live\n *   - adjacent free chunks merge eagerly on the second unref\n *   - non-adjacent frees stay separate\n *   - alloc on empty class falls through to a larger class\n *   - alloc above all declared sizes triggers growth\n *   - sweep merges runs of contiguous free chunks\n *   - duplicate sizes in the declaration get summed\n *   - 8-thread concurrent alloc/unref stress\n *\n * Designed in issue 302's rewrite; first stage of the unified\n * allocator implementation.\n */\n\n#include \"../src/016-unified-allocator.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int pass = 0;\nstatic int fail = 0;\n\n#define CHECK(cond, msg, ...) do {                                      \\\n    if (!(cond)) {                                                      \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"  FAIL: \" msg \" (%s:%d)\\n\",                    \\\n                ##__VA_ARGS__, __FILE__, __LINE__);                     \\\n        fail++;                                                         \\\n        return;                                                         \\\n    }                                                                   \\\n} while (0)\n\n#define PASS(name) do { pass++; printf(\"  ok   %s\\n\", name); } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_empty_heap */\nstatic void test_empty_heap(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"empty heap create/destroy\";\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(NULL, 0);\n    CHECK(h != NULL, \"ua_create with no classes returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 0, \"expected 0 regions, got %u\",\n          ua_region_count(h));\n    CHECK(ua_bytes_total(h) == 0, \"expected 0 total bytes\");\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_prewarming */\nstatic void test_prewarming(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"pre-warmed classes populate free-lists\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64,  .prewarm_count = 4 },\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 2 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h != NULL, \"ua_create failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 1, \"expected 1 region, got %u\",\n          ua_region_count(h));\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 4,\n          \"expected 4 free 64-byte chunks, got %u\",\n          ua_class_free_count(h, 64));\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 256) == 2,\n          \"expected 2 free 256-byte chunks, got %u\",\n          ua_class_free_count(h, 256));\n    CHECK(ua_alloc_calls(h) == 0, \"no allocs yet\");\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_alloc_pop_from_free_list */\nstatic void test_alloc_pop_from_free_list(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc pops from the matching class\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 2 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h != NULL, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 32);  /* fits in 64-byte class */\n    CHECK(a != NULL, \"alloc returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_size(a) >= 32, \"chunk too small\");\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 1, \"expected 1 left, got %u\",\n          ua_class_free_count(h, 64));\n\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(b != NULL, \"second alloc returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 0, \"expected 0 left\");\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 0, \"should not have grown\");\n\n    /* Distinct pointers — payloads don't overlap. */\n    CHECK(ua_data(a) != ua_data(b), \"two allocs gave same address\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_reuse_after_unref */\nstatic void test_reuse_after_unref(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc reuses a freed chunk without growing\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 128, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 128);\n    void       *pa = ua_data(a);\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 128);\n    CHECK(ua_data(b) == pa, \"expected same pointer back\");\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 0, \"should not have grown\");\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_refcount_keeps_alive */\nstatic void test_refcount_keeps_alive(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"ua_ref prevents free on first unref\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_ref(a);                 /* refcount = 2 */\n    ua_unref(h, a);            /* refcount = 1 — still live */\n\n    /* Trying to alloc again should NOT return `a`'s address — `a` is still\n     * in use. */\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(b != a, \"alloc reclaimed a chunk that still has a ref\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, a);            /* refcount = 0 — now freed */\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_adjacent_merge */\nstatic void test_adjacent_merge(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"two adjacent frees merge into one larger chunk\";\n    /* Carve 3 chunks of size 64 contiguously in one region. */\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 3 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    /* Take all three. Their payloads are in some order; we'll free\n     * them in physical-address order to trigger merging. */\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(a && b && c, \"alloc failed\");\n\n    /* Free a and b. They might or might not be physically adjacent\n     * depending on the order ua_alloc returns them. The free-list is\n     * LIFO, so the last-pushed is the first-popped. The test isn't\n     * sensitive to which physical order we got — we just need to\n     * verify that whichever two are adjacent merge when both freed. */\n    uint32_t merges_before = ua_neighbor_merges(h);\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_unref(h, c);\n\n    /* After all three free, at minimum some neighbor merges should\n     * have happened (three physically adjacent chunks can fuse). */\n    CHECK(ua_neighbor_merges(h) > merges_before,\n          \"expected at least one neighbor merge, got %u\",\n          ua_neighbor_merges(h) - merges_before);\n\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_non_adjacent_stay_separate */\nstatic void test_non_adjacent_stay_separate(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"non-adjacent frees do not merge\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 3 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n\n    /* Free outermost; keep middle (whichever it is in physical\n     * order). We don't know which is middle in physical order from\n     * the API, so this test instead verifies a weaker but useful\n     * property: freeing only `a` produces no merges (the other two\n     * are still allocated, so no neighbors are free). */\n    uint32_t before = ua_neighbor_merges(h);\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    CHECK(ua_neighbor_merges(h) == before,\n          \"expected no merges with neighbors allocated\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_unref(h, c);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_fallthrough_to_larger_class */\nstatic void test_fallthrough_to_larger_class(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc falls through to a larger class when small one is empty\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64,  .prewarm_count = 1 },\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    /* Exhaust the 64 class. */\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(a, \"first alloc failed\");\n\n    /* Now ask for 64 again. Should NOT grow — should fall through\n     * to the 256 class. */\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(b, \"second alloc failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 0, \"expected no growth, got %u\",\n          ua_grow_calls(h));\n    CHECK(ua_size(b) >= 64, \"chunk too small\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_growth_for_oversize */\nstatic void test_growth_for_oversize(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc above all classes triggers growth\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 1, \"should start with 1 region\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *big = ua_alloc(h, 4096);\n    CHECK(big, \"oversized alloc returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_size(big) >= 4096, \"chunk smaller than requested\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 2, \"expected 2 regions after growth, got %u\",\n          ua_region_count(h));\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 1, \"expected 1 grow call\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, big);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_explicit_sweep_merges_runs */\nstatic void test_explicit_sweep_merges_runs(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"ua_sweep merges what eager merge couldn't catch\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 4 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *chunks[4];\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) chunks[i] = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n\n    /* Free all four. Eager merge will catch most of this. The\n     * explicit sweep should be a no-op or near-no-op (since eager\n     * already did the work). The point of the test is that calling\n     * ua_sweep is safe and reports a sane count. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) ua_unref(h, chunks[i]);\n\n    uint32_t sweep_count = ua_sweep(h);\n    CHECK(sweep_count == 0, \"expected 0 extra merges after eager already ran, got %u\",\n          sweep_count);\n\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_duplicate_size_sums_count */\nstatic void test_duplicate_size_sums_count(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"duplicate class sizes sum their prewarm counts\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 2 },\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 3 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 5,\n          \"expected 5 (2+3), got %u\", ua_class_free_count(h, 64));\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Concurrent stress */\ntypedef struct stress_arg {\n    ua_t    *h;\n    int      n_ops;\n    _Atomic uint32_t *write_failures;\n} stress_arg_t;\n\nstatic void *stress_worker(void *arg_)\n{\n    stress_arg_t *arg = arg_;\n    for (int i = 0; i < arg->n_ops; i++) {\n        size_t sz = 16 + (size_t)(rand() % 240);\n        ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(arg->h, sz);\n        if (!c) {\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(arg->write_failures, 1u,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            continue;\n        }\n        /* Write the chunk to test no-overlap. */\n        memset(ua_data(c), 0xAB, ua_size(c));\n        /* Random hold pattern — sometimes ref-then-unref-twice. */\n        if (i % 3 == 0) {\n            ua_ref(c);\n            ua_unref(arg->h, c);\n        }\n        ua_unref(arg->h, c);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic void test_concurrent_stress(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"8-thread alloc/unref stress (1000 ops each)\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64,  .prewarm_count = 32 },\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 16 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    _Atomic uint32_t failures = 0;\n    pthread_t       threads[8];\n    stress_arg_t    args[8];\n    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {\n        args[i].h              = h;\n        args[i].n_ops          = 1000;\n        args[i].write_failures = &failures;\n        pthread_create(&threads[i], NULL, stress_worker, &args[i]);\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) pthread_join(threads[i], NULL);\n\n    CHECK(failures == 0, \"saw %u alloc failures during stress\",\n          (uint32_t)failures);\n    CHECK(ua_bytes_in_use(h) == 0,\n          \"expected 0 bytes in use after stress, got %llu\",\n          (unsigned long long)ua_bytes_in_use(h));\n\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_ua_data_writes_persist */\nstatic void test_ua_data_writes_persist(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"chunk payload survives across the API boundary\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(h, 200);\n    CHECK(c, \"alloc failed\");\n    uint8_t *d = ua_data(c);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) d[i] = (uint8_t)(i & 0xFF);\n\n    /* Round-trip check: write a pattern, read it back. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) {\n        CHECK(d[i] == (uint8_t)(i & 0xFF), \"byte %d corrupted\", i);\n    }\n    ua_unref(h, c);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"016-unified-allocator-test:\\n\");\n    test_empty_heap();\n    test_prewarming();\n    test_alloc_pop_from_free_list();\n    test_reuse_after_unref();\n    test_refcount_keeps_alive();\n    test_adjacent_merge();\n    test_non_adjacent_stay_separate();\n    test_fallthrough_to_larger_class();\n    test_growth_for_oversize();\n    test_explicit_sweep_merges_runs();\n    test_duplicate_size_sums_count();\n    test_ua_data_writes_persist();\n    test_concurrent_stress();\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", pass, fail);\n    return fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "content":"/* tests/016-unified-allocator-test.c — exercises the unified\n * allocator's contract end-to-end. Each test is independent (its\n * own heap), so failures isolate cleanly.\n *\n * What's covered:\n *   - empty-heap create/destroy round-trip\n *   - pre-warming: declared sizes produce ready-to-pop chunks\n *   - alloc + unref reuses chunks (no growth)\n *   - reference counting: extra ref keeps chunk live\n *   - adjacent free chunks merge eagerly on the second unref\n *   - non-adjacent frees stay separate\n *   - alloc on empty class falls through to a larger class\n *   - alloc above all declared sizes triggers growth\n *   - sweep merges runs of contiguous free chunks\n *   - duplicate sizes in the declaration get summed\n *   - 8-thread concurrent alloc/unref stress\n *\n * Designed in issue 302's rewrite; first stage of the unified\n * allocator implementation.\n */\n\n#include \"../src/016-unified-allocator.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int pass = 0;\nstatic int fail = 0;\n\n#define CHECK(cond, msg, ...) do {                                      \\\n    if (!(cond)) {                                                      \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"  FAIL: \" msg \" (%s:%d)\\n\",                    \\\n                ##__VA_ARGS__, __FILE__, __LINE__);                     \\\n        fail++;                                                         \\\n        return;                                                         \\\n    }                                                                   \\\n} while (0)\n\n#define PASS(name) do { pass++; printf(\"  ok   %s\\n\", name); } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_empty_heap */\nstatic void test_empty_heap(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"empty heap create/destroy\";\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(NULL, 0);\n    CHECK(h != NULL, \"ua_create with no classes returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 0, \"expected 0 regions, got %u\",\n          ua_region_count(h));\n    CHECK(ua_bytes_total(h) == 0, \"expected 0 total bytes\");\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_prewarming */\nstatic void test_prewarming(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"pre-warmed classes populate free-lists\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64,  .prewarm_count = 4 },\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 2 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h != NULL, \"ua_create failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 1, \"expected 1 region, got %u\",\n          ua_region_count(h));\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 4,\n          \"expected 4 free 64-byte chunks, got %u\",\n          ua_class_free_count(h, 64));\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 256) == 2,\n          \"expected 2 free 256-byte chunks, got %u\",\n          ua_class_free_count(h, 256));\n    CHECK(ua_alloc_calls(h) == 0, \"no allocs yet\");\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_alloc_pop_from_free_list */\nstatic void test_alloc_pop_from_free_list(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc pops from the matching class\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 2 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h != NULL, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 32);  /* fits in 64-byte class */\n    CHECK(a != NULL, \"alloc returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_size(a) >= 32, \"chunk too small\");\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 1, \"expected 1 left, got %u\",\n          ua_class_free_count(h, 64));\n\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(b != NULL, \"second alloc returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 0, \"expected 0 left\");\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 0, \"should not have grown\");\n\n    /* Distinct pointers — payloads don't overlap. */\n    CHECK(ua_data(a) != ua_data(b), \"two allocs gave same address\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_reuse_after_unref */\nstatic void test_reuse_after_unref(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc reuses a freed chunk without growing\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 128, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 128);\n    void       *pa = ua_data(a);\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 128);\n    CHECK(ua_data(b) == pa, \"expected same pointer back\");\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 0, \"should not have grown\");\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_refcount_keeps_alive */\nstatic void test_refcount_keeps_alive(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"ua_ref prevents free on first unref\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_ref(a);                 /* refcount = 2 */\n    ua_unref(h, a);            /* refcount = 1 — still live */\n\n    /* Trying to alloc again should NOT return `a`'s address — `a` is still\n     * in use. */\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(b != a, \"alloc reclaimed a chunk that still has a ref\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, a);            /* refcount = 0 — now freed */\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_adjacent_merge */\nstatic void test_adjacent_merge(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"two adjacent frees merge into one larger chunk\";\n    /* Carve 3 chunks of size 64 contiguously in one region. */\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 3 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    /* Take all three. Their payloads are in some order; we'll free\n     * them in physical-address order to trigger merging. */\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(a && b && c, \"alloc failed\");\n\n    /* Free a and b. They might or might not be physically adjacent\n     * depending on the order ua_alloc returns them. The free-list is\n     * LIFO, so the last-pushed is the first-popped. The test isn't\n     * sensitive to which physical order we got — we just need to\n     * verify that whichever two are adjacent merge when both freed. */\n    uint32_t merges_before = ua_neighbor_merges(h);\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_unref(h, c);\n\n    /* After all three free, at minimum some neighbor merges should\n     * have happened (three physically adjacent chunks can fuse). */\n    CHECK(ua_neighbor_merges(h) > merges_before,\n          \"expected at least one neighbor merge, got %u\",\n          ua_neighbor_merges(h) - merges_before);\n\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_non_adjacent_stay_separate */\nstatic void test_non_adjacent_stay_separate(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"non-adjacent frees do not merge\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 3 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n\n    /* Free outermost; keep middle (whichever it is in physical\n     * order). We don't know which is middle in physical order from\n     * the API, so this test instead verifies a weaker but useful\n     * property: freeing only `a` produces no merges (the other two\n     * are still allocated, so no neighbors are free). */\n    uint32_t before = ua_neighbor_merges(h);\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    CHECK(ua_neighbor_merges(h) == before,\n          \"expected no merges with neighbors allocated\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_unref(h, c);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_fallthrough_to_larger_class */\nstatic void test_fallthrough_to_larger_class(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc falls through to a larger class when small one is empty\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64,  .prewarm_count = 1 },\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    /* Exhaust the 64 class. */\n    ua_chunk_t *a = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(a, \"first alloc failed\");\n\n    /* Now ask for 64 again. Should NOT grow — should fall through\n     * to the 256 class. */\n    ua_chunk_t *b = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n    CHECK(b, \"second alloc failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 0, \"expected no growth, got %u\",\n          ua_grow_calls(h));\n    CHECK(ua_size(b) >= 64, \"chunk too small\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, a);\n    ua_unref(h, b);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_growth_for_oversize */\nstatic void test_growth_for_oversize(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"alloc above all classes triggers growth\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 1, \"should start with 1 region\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *big = ua_alloc(h, 4096);\n    CHECK(big, \"oversized alloc returned NULL\");\n    CHECK(ua_size(big) >= 4096, \"chunk smaller than requested\");\n    CHECK(ua_region_count(h) == 2, \"expected 2 regions after growth, got %u\",\n          ua_region_count(h));\n    CHECK(ua_grow_calls(h) == 1, \"expected 1 grow call\");\n\n    ua_unref(h, big);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_explicit_sweep_merges_runs */\nstatic void test_explicit_sweep_merges_runs(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"ua_sweep merges what eager merge couldn't catch\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 4 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *chunks[4];\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) chunks[i] = ua_alloc(h, 64);\n\n    /* Free all four. Eager merge will catch most of this. The\n     * explicit sweep should be a no-op or near-no-op (since eager\n     * already did the work). The point of the test is that calling\n     * ua_sweep is safe and reports a sane count. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) ua_unref(h, chunks[i]);\n\n    uint32_t sweep_count = ua_sweep(h);\n    CHECK(sweep_count == 0, \"expected 0 extra merges after eager already ran, got %u\",\n          sweep_count);\n\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_duplicate_size_sums_count */\nstatic void test_duplicate_size_sums_count(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"duplicate class sizes sum their prewarm counts\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 2 },\n        { .size = 64, .prewarm_count = 3 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n    CHECK(ua_class_free_count(h, 64) == 5,\n          \"expected 5 (2+3), got %u\", ua_class_free_count(h, 64));\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Concurrent stress */\ntypedef struct stress_arg {\n    ua_t    *h;\n    int      n_ops;\n    _Atomic uint32_t *write_failures;\n} stress_arg_t;\n\nstatic void *stress_worker(void *arg_)\n{\n    stress_arg_t *arg = arg_;\n    for (int i = 0; i < arg->n_ops; i++) {\n        size_t sz = 16 + (size_t)(rand() % 240);\n        ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(arg->h, sz);\n        if (!c) {\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(arg->write_failures, 1u,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            continue;\n        }\n        /* Write the chunk to test no-overlap. */\n        memset(ua_data(c), 0xAB, ua_size(c));\n        /* Random hold pattern — sometimes ref-then-unref-twice. */\n        if (i % 3 == 0) {\n            ua_ref(c);\n            ua_unref(arg->h, c);\n        }\n        ua_unref(arg->h, c);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic void test_concurrent_stress(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"8-thread alloc/unref stress (1000 ops each)\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 64,  .prewarm_count = 32 },\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 16 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 2);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    _Atomic uint32_t failures = 0;\n    pthread_t       threads[8];\n    stress_arg_t    args[8];\n    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {\n        args[i].h              = h;\n        args[i].n_ops          = 1000;\n        args[i].write_failures = &failures;\n        pthread_create(&threads[i], NULL, stress_worker, &args[i]);\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) pthread_join(threads[i], NULL);\n\n    CHECK(failures == 0, \"saw %u alloc failures during stress\",\n          (uint32_t)failures);\n    CHECK(ua_bytes_in_use(h) == 0,\n          \"expected 0 bytes in use after stress, got %llu\",\n          (unsigned long long)ua_bytes_in_use(h));\n\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_ua_data_writes_persist */\nstatic void test_ua_data_writes_persist(void)\n{\n    const char *name = \"chunk payload survives across the API boundary\";\n    ua_class_decl_t classes[] = {\n        { .size = 256, .prewarm_count = 1 },\n    };\n    ua_t *h = ua_create(classes, 1);\n    CHECK(h, \"create failed\");\n\n    ua_chunk_t *c = ua_alloc(h, 200);\n    CHECK(c, \"alloc failed\");\n    uint8_t *d = ua_data(c);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) d[i] = (uint8_t)(i & 0xFF);\n\n    /* Round-trip check: write a pattern, read it back. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) {\n        CHECK(d[i] == (uint8_t)(i & 0xFF), \"byte %d corrupted\", i);\n    }\n    ua_unref(h, c);\n    ua_destroy(h);\n    PASS(name);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"016-unified-allocator-test:\\n\");\n    test_empty_heap();\n    test_prewarming();\n    test_alloc_pop_from_free_list();\n    test_reuse_after_unref();\n    test_refcount_keeps_alive();\n    test_adjacent_merge();\n    test_non_adjacent_stay_separate();\n    test_fallthrough_to_larger_class();\n    test_growth_for_oversize();\n    test_explicit_sweep_merges_runs();\n    test_duplicate_size_sums_count();\n    test_ua_data_writes_persist();\n    test_concurrent_stress();\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", pass, fail);\n    return fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
